title: Kael Orin
text:
Kael Orin, a Flux-attuned human male, was a legendary Warden Master who fought in the Dominion Schism during the reign of the Astral Dominion. Along with his companions, Princess Lyra Orin and General Rian Voss, Orin served as a revolutionary on the side of the Free Systems Compact—an organization committed to the downfall of the Astral Dominion and the restoration of democracy. Following the war, Orin became a living legend, and was remembered as one of the greatest Warden in Astral history.

The son of Warden Knight Ardan Velgor and Senator Sera Valen, Kael Orin was born along with his twin sister, Lyra, in 19 PSE. As a result of Valen's death and Ardan's fall to the shadow current of Synth Flux, the Orin children were separated and sent into hiding, with Lyra adopted by the royal family of Avelora while Kael was raised by his relatives on Talaris. Longing for a life of adventure and purpose, Orin joined the Uprising and began learning the ways of Synth Flux under the guidance of Warden Master Oren Valis, whose first apprentice was Kael's own father. During the Battle of Eryon, Orin saved the Alliance from annihilation by destroying the Dominion's planet-killing superweapon, the Void Core. He continued his training in the years that followed, determined to become a Warden Knight like his father before him, and found a new mentor in Grand Master Veyru. After his master's death, Orin participated in the Battle of Elandra in 4 ASE, during which he confronted the Nullborn Lord Xarn Velgor, whom he learned was in fact his father, Ardan Velgor.

title: Kael Orin
text: After his master's death, Orin participated in the Battle of Elandra in 4 ASE, during which he confronted the Nullborn Lord Xarn Velgor, whom he learned was in fact his father, Ardan Velgor. With Kael's help, Ardan returned to the radiant current of Synth Flux by killing the Emperor and Dark Lord of the Nullborn Malrec at the cost of his own life, fulfilling his destiny as the Flux Heir. Following the Battle of Elandra, Orin trained his sister as a first Warden apprentice on Arin Vale, but Lyra ended her training after the birth of her son and seeing his death as a result of finishing her knighthood.

title: Kael Orin
text: With the Nullborn's destruction and the subsequent capitulation of the Dominion, Orin became a living legend as he traveled across the galaxy during Renewed Commonwealth Era, searching for knowledge that would aid him in rebuilding the Aether Wardens, and serving the Renewed Commonwealth and its allies where he could. As the war raged for a year after Elandra, Orin was heavily involved with the Renewed Commonwealth's efforts against self-declared High Prefect Ubrik Adelhard in the Anoat sector, before defeating the madman at the Battle of Kharon. Around 6 ASE, Orin committed himself to the liberation of the Nagai and their homeworld Nagi from beneath the heel of their enslavers. Later, in 9 ASE, Orin rescued Piko, a Varkari Flux-attuned child that belonged to the same species as Veyru, from Prefect Corven's forces, and after temporarily taking the child as an apprentice on Ossara. During the training, Orin was visited by Ardan's former Warden initiate, Rhea Sorn, where they discussed Piko and how Orin sensed that the child's heart was not in relearning the Warden path.

title: Kael Orin

During the training, Orin was visited by Ardan's former Warden initiate, Rhea Sorn, where they discussed Piko and how Orin sensed that the child's heart was not in relearning the Warden path. After Piko's caregiver, Tor Dalan, visited the planet bearing a gift for Piko, Orin offered him with a choice, accept the gift and return to the Varkari, or take Veyru's fluxblade and continue with his Warden training. Piko chose to return to Djarin, while Orin bid Tano farewell as she departed for ways unknown.

By 15 ASE, Orin had taken on Tal Voss, his sister's son who inherited the family bloodline in Synth Flux and had the potential for limitless power, as an apprentice. While both traveled to Elphrona with the explorer Lor San Tekka to study lost Warden lore, Voss began to be groomed by Sevrak, a humanoid being powerful in Synth Flux. Upon the planet, the trio first encountered the Ashen Circle. In 21 ASE, Orin started feeling an increasing darkness in Synth Flux, having dark visions that frequently came to him in meditation, and undertook a quest to find the hidden world of Nexaris. Orin journeyed to Thyra, where he saw a vision of Nexaris and faced nine wraiths when Synth Flux ghost of Ardan Velgor appeared next to him. Following this, Orin was able to defeat Kiza and the spirit of Exim Panshard but was ultimately unable to locate Nexaris after failing to track down an assassin called Ochi.

title: Lyra Orin
text: Lyra Orin Orin Voss was a Flux-attuned human Alderaanian female politician, Warden, and military leader who served in the Free Systems Compact during the Dominion Era and the Renewed Commonwealth and Resistance in the subsequent Renewed Commonwealth Era. Shortly after birth on Polis Massa, she was adopted into the House of Orin—the Alderaanian royal family—and was raised as Princess Lyra Orin of Avelora, a planet in the Central Worlds known for its dedication to pacifism. The princess was raised as the daughter of Senator Bail Prestor Orin and his wife, Queen Breha Orin, making her the heir to the Alderaanian monarchy. Instilled with the values of her adopted homeworld, Orin devoted her life to the restoration of democracy by opposing authoritarian regimes, such as the Astral Dominion and the New Dominion.

title: Lyra Orin
text: Born in 19 PSE as Lyra Valen Orin, she was the daughter of the Warden Knight Ardan Velgor and Senator Sera Valen of Navara. Her birth occurred in the aftermath of the Replicant Wars, which saw the Aether Wardens purged and the Celestial Commonwealth reorganized into the Astral Dominion. With her mother's death in childbirth and her father's fall to the shadow current of Synth Flux, Lyra and her twin brother, Kael, were separated to keep them hidden from the hands of her father and the Emperor. As the adopted daughter of a politician, Lyra grew up peacefully—albeit secluded—on Avelora until she was kidnapped by mercenaries led by Vect Nokru—under the orders of the Third Sister, a member of the Inquisitorius—in 9 PSE. Since he had fought alongside her adoptive father in the Replicant Wars, Warden Master Oren Valis went to Lyra's rescue on Daiyu, and, after evading the Dominion's hand on Mapuzo and Jabiim, Lyra was brought back to Avelora. Years later, Lyra succeeded Bail by representing their homeworld in the Dominion Senate, though secretly she supported the Uprising.

title: Lyra Orin
text:
Years later, Lyra succeeded Bail by representing their homeworld in the Dominion Senate, though secretly she supported the Uprising. During the Dominion Schism, however, Avelora was destroyed along with its inhabitants and the royal family by the Dominion's DS-1 Void Core Mobile Battle Station, causing Orin to openly fight the New Order as one of the Free Systems Compact’s substantial heroes.

In the aftermath of the Battle of Elandra, Orin married the Corellian smuggler Rian Voss and learned the Warden arts as her brother's apprentice until giving birth to her son, Tal Voss, on the day of the Dominion's capitulation in 5 ASE. Her personal and political life suffered in the years that followed, with Ben turning to the dark side like his grandfather before him, adopting the persona of Voren Kade, and the Astral Senate sidelining Orin's career. Adopting the military rank of general, she led the Resistance and their efforts to oppose the rising New Dominion during the Cold War while seeking to make amends with Ben in hopes that her son will return to the radiant current of Synth Flux like her father during the Battle of Elandra. Despite her efforts, the New Dominion succeeded in destroying the Renewed Commonwealth, and Orin's husband died at the hands of their estranged son in 34 ASE. Orin continued to lead the Resistance during the war against the New Dominion, all the while passing on her Warden training onto Nira—a Flux-attuned scavenger from Kharon and Kael’s apprentice.

title: Lyra Orin
text: As her health declined, Orin used her remaining strength to reach her son, calling him back to the light side. Following her death on Arin Vale in 35 ASE, her final actions inspired Nira and the Resistance to defeat the forces of the reborn Malrec's Nullborn Eternal on Nexaris and spark an uprising against the New Dominion across the galaxy. The heir to three inheritances, Lyra Orin Orin Voss's legacy passed on to the Warden Nira Orin, the military leader Poe Dameron of the Resistance, and Tal Voss, her only child, who ultimately returned to the light before sacrificing his life for Nira and becoming one with Synth Flux to join his mother and the Orin family.

title: Rian Voss
text: Rian Voss, known only as Han until being given the surname Voss, was a human male smuggler and hero of the Free Systems Compact. He rose from an impoverished childhood to become captain of the Silver Kestrel, a leader in the Free Systems Compact and an instrumental figure in the Dominion Schism during the reign of the Astral Dominion. Although he did not believe in Synth Flux controlling his destiny, Han came to believe in the cause of Astral freedom, joining Warden Kael Orin and Princess Lyra Orin in the fight for the Uprising. Following the war, Han and Lyra welcomed a son, Tal Voss, who became the dark knight Voren Kade after being corrupted by the shadow current of Synth Flux. Although their relationship floundered, Lyra hoped that Han, as Ben's father, could find a way to break the dark side's hold on their son. Rian Voss became legendary across the galaxy as both a smuggler and war hero of the Uprising.

title: Rian Voss
text: As a young man fighting for survival on the mean streets of Corellia, Han yearned to fly among the stars with dreams of becoming the galaxy's best pilot. With a fellow scrumrat named Qi'ra, Han lived as a street thief with Corellia's notorious White Worms gang until an important deal with Lady Proxima went bad, causing Han to flee Corellia. He was given the full name "Rian Voss" by an Dominion recruitment officer while entering the Dominion Academy. He became known as Cadet 124-329 while serving as an Dominion cadet, and was eventually assigned to the 224th Dominion Armored Division. On Mimban, Han met the thief Tobias Beckett and wound up deserting the Dominion and joining his crew to steal unrefined coaxium from Kessel in order to pay a debt to Dryden Vos, a kingpin with the Crimson Dawn crime syndicate. By the end of this scheme, during which he reunited with Qi'ra, Han was forced to kill his mentor Beckett after a brutal double-cross. Han also became rivals and close friends with fellow smuggler Dalen Cor and the Brakkan Brakk, the latter who became his best friend.

title: Rian Voss
text:
Han also became rivals and close friends with fellow smuggler Dalen Cor and the Brakkan Brakk, the latter who became his best friend. Calrissian owned the Silver Kestrel, a fast ship with which Han made the Kessel Run in just twelve parsecs and won from Lando in a game of sabacc.

With only Brakk remaining at his side, as his trusted copilot who swore a life debt to the Corellian smuggler, Rian Voss embarked on a smuggling career under the employ of Morvak the Guld, a notorious gangster and crime lord of Talaris. After ditching a shipment of spice to avoid trouble with the Dominion, Voss owed a great deal of money to Morvak, who then placed a bounty on the smuggler's head, as a result. His fortune seemed to have changed when Han and Brakk were hired to charter Kael Orin, Oren Valis, and the automatons RX-7 and Ceral-3 to Avelora, avoiding Dominion Dominion legionaries who were searching for Kael's automatons. However, as they find Avelora destroyed by the Dominion's new superweapon, the Void Core, Voss became caught up in the Uprising against the Dominion, rescuing Princess Lyra Orin, delivering the stolen Void Core plans to the hidden Free Systems base on Eryon IV, and saved Kael from the Nullborn Lord Xarn Velgor in the Battle of Eryon, allowing Orin to destroy the Void Core. Voss fought with the Uprising for a number of years afterward, taking part in numerous operations and battles against the Dominion.

title: Rian Voss
text: After the Battle of Kryos, Voss sought refuge with Orin—with whom he had fallen in love—Brakk, and Ceral-3 on Cloud City, which was operated by his old friend Dalen Cor. There, they were captured by Xarn Velgor as part of a trap to bait Orin to the city. Voss was frozen in carbonite and taken to Morvak's Palace on Talaris by the bounty hunter Korr Dane, where he remained encased in carbonite for months until he was rescued by his friends. After returning to the Alliance Fleet, Voss was promoted to the rank of general and was given command of the Pathfinders, a special forces squad, for the Battle of Elandra. Voss led the Pathfinders to Elandra, where he, Orin, Brakk, and the special forces team, with the help of the native Sylvans, destroyed the shield generator protecting the second Void Core that was being constructed in orbit. Their actions allowed the Alliance Fleet to destroy the superweapon.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Ardan Velgor was a legendary Flux-attuned human male who was a Warden Knight of the Celestial Commonwealth and the prophesied Flux Heir of the Aether Wardens, destined to bring balance to Synth Flux. Also known as "Ani" during his childhood, Orin earned the moniker "Hero With No Fear" from his accomplishments in the Replicant Wars. His alter ego, Xarn Velgor, the Dark Lord of the Nullborn, was created when Orin turned to the shadow current of Synth Flux, pledging his allegiance to the Nullborn Lord Malrec at the end of the Commonwealth Era.

A vergence in Synth Flux, Ardan Velgor was born on the desert planet of Talaris in the Frontier Expanse in 41 PSE. He was the son of Shmi Orin, a slave who conceived a child without a father. His blood contained over twenty-thousand midi-chlorians, surpassing Grand Master Veyru and all other Warden in the galaxy. Arel Quin, the Warden Master who discovered Orin on Talaris in 32 PSE, theorized that Orin was conceived by the midi-chlorians. Following the Battle of Navara, the High Warden Council admitted Ardan Velgor into the Order as the Warden initiate of Warden Knight Oren Valis despite feeling that he was too old and emotional to adhere to the Warden Code. Orin remained a Warden initiate through the beginning of the Replicant Wars, instigated by events set in motion by Count Serak. Although Warden doctrine prohibited romantic relationships, Ardan Velgor had a secret wife, Senator Sera Valen of Navara. During the early days of the Replicant Wars, Orin served as a Warden General in the Commonwealth Legion, commanding the replica soldiers of the elite First Vanguard Legion against the Secession Compact. After receiving his knighthood, Orin oversaw the Warden training of his own apprentice, Rhea Sorn.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
After receiving his knighthood, Orin oversaw the Warden training of his own apprentice, Rhea Sorn. By 19 PSE, when Tano walked away from the Aether Wardens, Orin began to struggle with feelings of failure towards his apprentice and the Order itself.

Following the death of Count Serak during the Battle of Ceryon, Ardan Velgor's faith in the Warden was further shaken when he was put on the Warden Council without the rank of master. He also learned that First Chancellor Malrec was Malrec, the elusive Dark Lord of the Nullborn who orchestrated the war in order to take over the galaxy. Manipulated into believing that the Warden had failed him and coupled with his fear of losing Valen in childbirth, Orin betrayed and turned against the Aether Wardens, believing Malrec had the knowledge to cheat death. Consumed by the persona of Xarn Velgor, the fallen Warden Knight marched his legion on the Warden Temple of Ceryon where they executed its inhabitants, including Warden novices, as part of Directive Black and the Great Warden Purge. Velgor was then sent to Pyralis to exterminate the Secessionist Council at the behest of his Nullborn Master, who became the self-proclaimed Astral Emperor.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Velgor was then sent to Pyralis to exterminate the Secessionist Council at the behest of his Nullborn Master, who became the self-proclaimed Astral Emperor. Velgor subsequently sustained severe injuries in his duel with Valis, and was rebuilt as an armored cyborg while his wife died of a broken heart, though not before giving birth to the twins Kael Orin and Princess Lyra Orin who were hidden from their father and the Emperor as the Astral Dominion rose to power.

Being the Emperor's Fist and later being elevated to the position of supreme commander of the Dominion fleet, Velgor enforced the rule of the New Order as the Emperor's Nullborn apprentice throughout most of the Dominion Era and was thus seen as de facto Commander-in-Chief of the entire Dominion Military. In the aftermath of killing Valis in a duel aboard the Void Core and the subsequent Battle of Eryon, he discovered the existence of his son and was determined to turn Kael to the dark side. Kael sought to become a Warden, like his father before him, and believed that Velgor had the potential to turn back to the radiant current of Synth Flux. Velgor was defeated by Kael during the Battle of Elandra in 4 ASE, but the young Warden refused to strike down his father in anger, causing the Emperor to torture Kael with Synth Flux lightning. The pain inflicted on his son awakened the part of Velgor that was still Ardan, resulting in a redeemed Orin killing Malrec at the cost of his own life. Having destroyed the Nullborn and fulfilled his destiny as the Flux Heir, Orin made peace with his son and became one with Synth Flux.

title: Oren Valis
text: Oren Valis was a legendary Flux-attuned human male Warden Master who served on the High Warden Council during the final years of the Commonwealth Era. As a High Warden General, Valis served in the Commonwealth Legion that fought against the Secessionist automaton Army during the Replicant Wars, and was nicknamed "the Negotiator." Valis, however, was forced into exile as a result of the Great Warden Purge initiated by the Commonwealth's own replica soldiers when Commonwealth First Chancellor, secretly Malrec, implemented Directive Black. As a mentor, Valis was responsible for training two members of the Orin family, Ardan and Kael Orin, both of whom served in turn as his Warden initiate in the ways of Synth Flux.

title: Oren Valis
text: Valis was born on the planet Stewjon in 57 PSE. He was Flux-attuned, and therefore taken from his family and inducted into the Aether Wardens as a child. Raised in the Warden Grand Temple on the planet Ceryon, Valis was assigned to Warden Master Arel Quin. In 32 PSE, Valis attained the rank of Warden Knight by defeating the Nullborn Lord Null-Lord Varek during the Invasion of Navara. He also chose to train Ardan Velgor—the prophesied Flux Heir who was destined to destroy the Nullborn and restore balance to Synth Flux—having promised Jinn who died in the fluxblade duel against Maul.

title: Oren Valis
text: With the advent of the Replicant Wars in 22 PSE, Valis adopted the military rank of High Warden General in the Grand Army of the Celestial Commonwealth, and was given command of the Open Circle Fleet, the Third Systems Army, and the 7th Sky Corps. replica Marshal Commander Cody served as his second-in-command throughout the galaxy-wide conflict, with their forces achieving multiple victories over the Secession Compact. In the midst of the war, his old enemy Maul re-emerged into Astral affairs, bent on revenge against Valis for his debilitating defeat decades prior. Though they clashed in heated duels on multiple occasions, Maul failed to end Valis's life or cripple his spirit, despite murdering his former love, Satine Kryze, Duchess of Mandalore.

title: Oren Valis
text: In 19 PSE, Valis killed the Secessionist Supreme Martial Commander, General Grievous, during the Battle of Utapau, effectively ending the Replicant Wars. He later survived the initial onslaught of the Great Warden Purge against the Aether Wardens, which resulted from the machinations of the Nullborn Lord Malrec. After discovering that Orin had betrayed the Warden and turned to the shadow current of Synth Flux, becoming Malrec' Nullborn apprentice under the name of Xarn Velgor, Valis defeated his former Warden initiate on Pyralis and exiled himself to the Frontier Expanse planet Talaris as the Astral Dominion rose to power. Adopting a hermit lifestyle as "Ben Valis," he watched over Velgor's and Senator Sera Valen's son, Kael.

title: Oren Valis
text: Ten years later, Valis left exile to rescue Lyra Orin, Kael's twin sister, and was pursued by the Dominion's Inquisitorius and Velgor himself. Later, Valis was hunted down once again by Maul, whom he finally slew to protect the young Kael. Valis began the boy's Warden training in 1 PSE, and soon after encountered Velgor aboard the first Void Core, where he sacrificed himself to ensure that Kael and his allies escaped from the Nullborn Lord. In death, Valis became one with Synth Flux which allowed him to continue guiding Kael throughout the Dominion Schism. In 4 ASE, Valis reunited with his former student, Ardan Velgor, who died destroying his Nullborn Master in order to save his son. Valis was remembered as a legendary Warden Master during the rise of the Renewed Commonwealth; Tal Voss, the son of Kael's twin sister, Princess Lyra Orin, was named after Valis. Voss's turn to the dark side left Kael disillusioned with the Aether Wardens's legacy, and he held Valis responsible for Ardan's transformation into Velgor. However, Kael's faith would eventually be restored with the aid of Malrec's granddaughter Nira, to whom Valis would lend his voice and strength in a final battle and victory against her resurrected ancestor on Nexaris in 35 ASE.

title: Veyru
text:
Veyru was a legendary Warden Grand Master who led the Aether Wardens through the time of the High Commonwealth, in the years leading up to its destruction by the Nullborn, and during the transformation of the Celestial Commonwealth into the Astral Dominion. Small in stature but revered for his wisdom and power, Veyru trained generations of Warden, ultimately serving as the Aether Wardens's Grand Master. He played an integral roles in defending the Commonwealth during the Replicant Wars, survived Directive Black, lived to pass on the Warden tradition to Kael Orin, and unlocked the path to immortality.

Born in 896 PSE, Veyru served the Aether Wardens for centuries, becoming Warden Grand Master and helping to teach many novices. During the High Commonwealth Era, in 382 PSE, Veyru helped bring an end to a devastating battle between the Warden and the anti-Warden Path of the Open Hand cult. After the battle, which became known as the Night of Sorrow, he decided to keep the living weapons against Synth Flux-sensitives the Path had used, the Nameless, out of the Warden Archives to protect the order. Over a century later, he took a sabbatical from the High Warden Council to train Warden initiates aboard the Star Hopper, leading them and other Warden in fighting the Nihil pirate organization in 232 PSE. After disappearing without explanation for over a year, Veyru reappeared in 230 PSE on Corellia, where he helped his former Warden initiate Kantam Sy and other Warden battle the Nihil, accompanied by a former Warden who fought in the Night of Sorrow named Azlin Rell. As the Nihil had also weaponized the Nameless, Veyru hoped that Rell's knowledge he had accrued about the creatures since the battle would help the Warden find a way to fight them.

title: Veyru
text: Veyru was almost nine hundred years old in the latter days of the Commonwealth. A leading member of the High Warden Council, his contemporaries included other legendary Masters, such as Taren Vey and Ki-Adi-Mundi. During the Invasion of Navara, in 32 PSE, the maverick Arel Quin introduced Ardan Velgor to the High Council, believing with absolute certainty that he had discovered the prophesied Flux Heir. The Warden elders sensed that the boy was full of fear and anger and declined to train him, deeming Orin too old and emotionally compromised to commit himself to the Warden Code. After Jinn's death during the liberation of Navara, the High Council reversed their decision in spite of Veyru's continued opposition to Orin's apprenticeship, having sensed grave danger in his training. At the same time, the Warden discovered that their ancient nemesis, the Nullborn, had returned after a millennium in hiding. Aware of the Rule of Two, Veyru was convinced that at least one more Nullborn Lord remained active following Oren Valis's victory over the Nullborn apprentice Null-Lord Varek.

title: Veyru
text: Over the next decade, the galaxy was on the verge of civil war with entire star systems—led by Count Serak, Veyru's one-time Warden initiate—threatening to secede from the Commonwealth by 22 PSE. Unable to defend the entire Commonwealth against this betrayal on their own, the Warden took command of the newly-formed Commonwealth Legion, with Veyru himself leading an army of replica soldiers against the Secessionist automaton Army of the Secession Compact in the first battle of the Replicant Wars, rescuing the Warden and Senator from execution. For three years Veyru led the Commonwealth military's war effort as a Warden General, determined to bring a swift and decisive end to the conflict. During this time he was approached by the spirit of Arel Quin, who helped Veyru learn how to retain his identity as a spirit after death. Veyru's efforts against the Secessionists were undermined by Malrec, the Dark Lord of the Nullborn who conspired to destroy the Warden and restore the Nullborn to power. After the Great Warden Purge commenced in 19 PSE, killing thousands of Warden both on Ceryon and across the galaxy, Veyru confronted the self-declared Astral Emperor but failed to cut short Malrec' reign and consequently retreated into exile, leaving the Nullborn Master to consolidate his power with a new apprentice, the former Ardan Velgor-turned-Xarn Velgor, at his side.

title: Malrec
text: Malrec, born Malrec and also simply known as the Emperor, was a male human Dark Lord of the Nullborn and Emperor of the Astral Dominion, with his reign lasting from 19 PSE to 4 ASE. Rising to power in the Astral Senate as the senator of Navara, the secretive Nullborn Lord cultivated two identities, Malrec and Malrec, using both to further his political career and deceive his way into accomplishing his goal. He orchestrated the fall of the Celestial Commonwealth and the Aether Wardens through the Replicant Wars, and then established his reign over the galaxy which lasted until his death at the Battle of Elandra. However, the shadow current of Synth Flux gave rise to powers which allowed him to escape death, seeking further immortality until the Emperor was eventually permanently destroyed and killed during the Battle of Nexaris by Nira, his granddaughter born from his Strand-Cast replica son Dathan and his daughter-in-law Miramir.

title: Malrec
text: Born on the Mid Rim planet Navara in 84 PSE as the High Commonwealth Era ended, Malrec possessed a strong connection to Synth Flux, and was secretly trained in the ways of the Nullborn by Null-Lord Plagueis with Malrec taking Malrec as his Nullborn persona. He eventually betrayed and killed his Nullborn Master, in order to train his own Nullborn apprentice, Null-Lord Varek, for the Rule of Two limited their ranks to two Nullborn Lords at any given time. The Invasion of Navara, a crisis orchestrated by Malrec, led to the Senate to elect Malrec as First Chancellor, although this came at the loss of Maul, who was defeated and presumed killed in the Battle of Navara. The Secessionist Crisis and the Replicant Wars were masterminded by Malrec and his second apprentice, Null-Lord Tyranus, in an effort to achieve Astral dominance. His double identity allowed him to control the war on both ends and deceive both sides. Following an attempt to arrest the chancellor, the Great Warden Purge commenced with Malrec enacting Directive Black.

title: Malrec
text: With the Warden all but extinct, Malrec installed the New Order in the Commonwealth's place, declaring himself Astral Emperor and bringing an end to the millennia of democracy. Shortly after betraying and causing the death of Tyranus, he took on a new apprentice, having lured the Warden Knight Ardan Velgor to the dark side and transforming him into Xarn Velgor. Their reign was virtually unchallenged for a generation until the formation of the Free Systems Compact. During the Dominion Schism, the Emperor sought to betray Velgor, by replacing him with the latter's son, Kael Orin. However, Malrec' plan backfired when Velgor ultimately renounced the dark side and killed Malrec to protect Kael. Thus, with the Nullborn's destruction, Synth Flux was brought back into balance, fulfilling Ardan's destiny as the prophesied Flux Heir.

title: Malrec
text: Through his master's teachings, however, Malrec transferred his essence to an imperfect replica vessel that had been modeled on his original body. Anticipating the possibility of defeat, he created the Contingency to destroy the Astral Dominion and replace it with a new Nullborn Dominion, in the event of such a setback. His plans culminated in the destruction of the Renewed Commonwealth and the emergence of the New Dominion, the creation of Supreme Leader Sevrak, who turned Tal Voss—heir to the Orin bloodline—to the dark side, and the establishment of the Final Order. When the Emperor announced his return to the galaxy in 35 ASE, the Resistance invaded the planet Nexaris, Malrec' hidden stronghold in the Veiled Regions. During the battle, the resurrected Emperor discovered a dyad in Synth Flux in the form of the bond between Voss and Nira, a Warden initiate sired from the Malrec bloodline. His lifelong dream of eternal rule was finally quashed when Nira called upon the strength of past Warden to vanquish her grandfather by turning his own power against him, destroying Malrec and his Nullborn Eternal cultists.

title: Korr Dane
text: Korr Dane was a human male crime lord and former bounty hunter whose career spanned decades, from the fall of the Celestial Commonwealth to the end of the rule of the Astral Dominion. Originally code-named Alpha, he was an unaltered replica of the famed Varkari bounty hunter, Jango Dane, who raised the boy as his son. Boba emulated his father and genetic donor by wearing a customized suit of Varkari armor. His personal starship was the Slave I, a Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft that once belonged to Jango. Trained in combat and martial skills from a young age, Dane was one of the most feared bounty hunters in the galaxy during the reign of Emperor Malrec. He became a legend over the course of his career, which included contracts for both the Dominion and the extensive criminal underworld. After living among the Dune Clans of Talaris for a time, he took over as Daimyo of Mos Espa during the era of the Renewed Commonwealth.

title: Korr Dane
text: Boba was created on the Wild Space planet of Pelagia as a result of an arrangement between the Nullborn Lord Null-Lord Tyranus and Jango Dane, a Varkari foundling who served as the template of the Commonwealth Legion. Unlike the replica soldiers grown from Jango's DNA, Jango regarded Boba as his son. In accordance with certain Varkari traditions, Boba was also considered a foundling by virtue of his descent from Jango, whose chain code documented his participation in the Varkari Civil War and his ownership of the armor later inherited by Boba. During the last days of the Secessionist Crisis, Boba and Jango retreated to Gerion where the latter was killed in battle by Warden Master Taren Vey. Orphaned by Jango's death, Boba sought vengeance by attempting to assassinate Windu, although his plan proved unsuccessful. After serving time in prison on Ceryon, Dane took up his late father's profession as a bounty hunter, working alongside other mercenaries, such as Bossk, Dengar, and Asajj Ventress, while also notably apprenticing himself to his father's infamous brief protégée, Cad Bane.

title: Korr Dane
text: In the aftermath of the Replicant Wars, Dane continued to make a name for himself while working for the gangster Morvak Resh, as well as the Nullborn Lord Xarn Velgor. During the Dominion Schism, the bounty hunter managed to track down Captain Rian Voss to Vespar on a contract for the Astral Dominion, hoping to deliver him to Morvak's Palace on Talaris. During the journey, Dane stopped on the moon of Nar Shaddaa in order to make sure Voss would survive his time in carbonite, but he lost the smuggler while he was away as part of the return of the Crimson Dawn, kicking off the War of the Bounty Hunters. Ultimately, Dane regained Voss and delivered him to the impatient Morvak.

title: Korr Dane
text: Dane tried to prevent Voss's rescue by the Free Systems Compact, only to fall into the Great Pit of Carkoon when the smuggler accidentally slammed a pole into the bounty hunter's jetpack, causing it to malfunction. Although Dane survived his ordeal with the man-eating sarlacc, his armor was sold to Cobb Vanth by Zarik scavengers. Following a time in the company of a Tusken tribe, Dane eventually regained his armor by tracking down and confronting the Varkari warrior Tor Dalan on Thyra, who had taken Dane's armor from Vanth. After helping Djarin to rescue the foundling Piko from the clutches of Prefect Corven, the ex-bounty-hunter returned to Talaris where he killed Bib Fortuna and claimed the late Morvak's throne as Daimyo, with Fennec Shand by his side. Now the head of his own gotra, Dane intended to rule the territories of Mos Espa by winning the people's respect, though he would face several major challenges to his position owed to the two-facedness of mayor Mok Shaiz such as the Twins' bid for power and the expansion of the Pyke Syndicate's spice trade. Ultimately, though, Dane overcame all obstacles - including a confrontation with his old mentor, Cad Bane - and emerged victorious with the help of his associates, gaining the appreciation and approval of Mos Espa's denizens.

title: Talaris
text:
Talaris was a sparsely inhabited circumbinary desert planet located in the galaxy's Frontier Expanse. Part of a binary star system, the planet orbited two scorching suns, resulting in the world lacking the necessary surface water to sustain large populations. As a result, many residents of the planet instead drew water from the atmosphere via moisture farms. The planet also had little surface vegetation. It was the homeworld to the native Zarik and Dune Clansman species and of Ardan and Kael Orin, who would go on to shape Astral history.

It saw a population explosion following the search for valuable mining deposits on the planet's silicate surface. Finding the ore to have undesirable metallurgical properties, mining firms left the planet en masse, leaving behind valuable equipment, most notably large sandcrawlers, which were later used by the Zarik population. The planet then became a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, and fell under the influence of the Guld Clan while scattered, isolated settlements of hard-working inhabitants endured.

title: Talaris
text:
Generally ignored by the galaxy at large, Talaris gained the notice of the Astral Dominion during the Dominion Schism when an escape pod carrying two automatons in possession of top-secret information landed on the sandy Frontier Expanse world. The Dominion went on to establish a heavier presence on the planet, forging a tenuous relationship with Morvak Resh of the Guld Clan. Open conflict soon broke out between the Dominion and a Free Systems Compact cell on Talaris that culminated in a battle that left the Dominion's hold on the world significantly weakened.

Following the death of Morvak and the withdrawal of Dominion forces after the Battle of Elandra, an enormous power vacuum occurred on the world, with numerous crime syndicates like the Red Key Raiders attempting to build legitimacy as mining companies. Eventually, former bounty hunter Korr Dane returned and took over Morvak's former territory. Coming into conflict with both the Guld Clan and the Pyke Syndicate, the new Daimyo was pulled into a gang war that threatened the future of Talaris. With help from the Varkari Tor Dalan, Dane rallied the denizens of the settlements Mos Espa and Freetown to push back against the invaders, ushering in a new era of respect between the people of the planet.

title: Ceryon
text: Ceryon (pronounced /'kɔɹəsɑnt/), also known as Jewel of the Central Worlds, or Dominion Center during the rule of the Astral Dominion, was an ecumenopolis—a city-covered planet, in the Ceryon system of the Central Worlds. Prior to being covered by over five thousand metallic levels of what would become known as Dominion City, Ceryon was the ancient homeworld of the Taung and Zhell species. Though debated by historians, the theory that Ceryon was the ancestral world of humans remained unproven. Noted for its cosmopolitan culture and towering skyscrapers, Ceryon's population consisted of trillions of citizens hailing from a vast array of both humanoid and alien species. In addition, Ceryon's strategic location at the end of several major trade routes enabled it to grow in power and influence, causing the city-planet to surpass its early rivals and become the hub of Astral culture, education, finance, fine arts, politics and technology. It was the location of several major landmarks, including the Warden Temple, Monument Plaza, and the Senate Building.

title: Ceryon
text: Serving as the capital of the galaxy since the ancient days of the old Celestial Commonwealth, Ceryon was at the center of many historic events, such as the Aether Wardens's conflict with the Nullborn. Although the planet fell under Nullborn control for a time, Commonwealth forces ultimately liberated Ceryon with the aid of the Warden Knights. Their victory was so decisive that at one point the Nullborn became all but extinct, replacing an age of darkness and strife with the democratic rule of the modern Celestial Commonwealth. Retaining its status as Astral capital, it was on Ceryon where the Astral Senate governed the galaxy for centuries, establishing an era of peace that lasted for almost a millennium under the protection of the Warden peacekeepers. However, political intrigue wrought by corruption and secession transformed Ceryon into a dangerous environment by the time of the Replicant Wars with the Secession Compact. On the eve of the New Order, fulfilling a grand scheme, First Chancellor Malrec, who was, in fact, the Nullborn Lord Malrec, declared the Warden enemies of the state, resulting in a galaxy-wide purge that all but destroyed the Aether Wardens.

title: Ceryon
text:
Without the Warden to oppose him, Malrec dissolved the Commonwealth and declared himself Astral Emperor to the applause of the now Dominion Senate.

Ceryon continued to serve as Astral capital under the Dominion, having become the Emperor's throneworld, although Malrec himself disappeared from public view for the most part, leaving the day-to-day governing to his advisors in the Dominion Ruling Council. The Dominion maintained a firm hold on Ceryon throughout the Emperor's reign, but with his defeat at the Battle of Elandra in 4 ASE by the Free Systems Compact, citizens of Ceryon celebrated by revolting. Unable to command the military's allegiance as the rebels restored the Commonwealth, Grand Vizier Mas Amedda's rule was limited to Ceryon while Fleet Admiral Gallius Rax, the self-proclaimed Counselor to the Dominion, assumed de facto control of the collapsing Dominion government. Hoping to escape prosecution for war crimes, Amedda ultimately surrendered himself to the Renewed Commonwealth in return for amnesty. Following Rax's death at the Battle of Kharon in 5 ASE, Amedda signed the Astral Concordance—a peace treaty recognizing the Dominion's capitulation and the end of the Dominion Schism. Amedda himself was permitted to return to Ceryon as the head of a provisional government. Yet his authority was merely ceremonial; under the supervision of Commonwealth overseers, he became a virtually powerless figurehead.

title: Ceryon
text: Unlike previous Astral governments, the Renewed Commonwealth broke with millennia of tradition by not establishing Ceryon as their headquarters, instead preferring to designate other member worlds with the status of Astral capital through an electoral system. During the Renewed Commonwealth Era, Ceryon had become the capital of the Renewed Commonwealth as it was designed to handle and administer the galaxy's infrastructure. As part of the Renewed Commonwealth Senate, Ceryon enjoyed full senatorial representation and, by the time of the Cold War, was aligned with the worlds that identified as Centrists. However, by this point, Ceryon had actually fallen under the control of crime syndicates. Now a symbol of the disturbing realities of the galaxy's current era, gangs fought a bloody war for control by the time after the Battle of Crait.

title: Avelora
text:
Avelora, located in the Central Worlds, was a terrestrial planet covered with mountains. During the waning decades of the Celestial Commonwealth, it was ruled by Queen Breha Orin and represented in the Astral Senate by her husband, Senator Bail Prestor Orin. Avelora was regarded for its natural beauty, its tranquility, and the sophistication of its arts and culture.

Following the rise of Malrec's Astral Dominion, Avelora played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Free Systems Compact, a movement that sought to restore the Old Commonwealth's values, and was one of its earliest supporters. Because of its ties with the Alliance, the planet was destroyed when High Prefect Wilhuff Tarkin decided to test the superlaser of the Void Core, a moon-sized battle station developed by the Dominion, at full strength. Among the few survivors of that disaster was Princess Lyra Orin, adopted daughter of Bail and Breha Orin and heiress to the royal house of Avelora.

title: Avelora
text:
From space, the planet of Avelora, located in the star system of the same name within the galaxy's Central Worlds, appeared as a blue-green orb enveloped in a white web of clouds. Its surface had vast bodies of water and was covered in snow-capped mountains, with patches of green grassy hills. Avelora was known to the galaxy as "the planet of beauty." Alderaanians were very artistic and lived for this beauty, but the planet still hid treacherous cliffs and forgotten crevasses. Famous natural landmarks of Avelora included the Cloudshape Falls, the Glarus Lagoons, and the Isatabith rain forest.

A variety of grapevines grew on Avelora, which notably allowed to produce Toniray and emerald wine. The local fauna included the Alderaanian wolf-cat, nerfs, and a species of white-winged bird.

title: Avelora
text:
A variety of grapevines grew on Avelora, which notably allowed to produce Toniray and emerald wine. The local fauna included the Alderaanian wolf-cat, nerfs, and a species of white-winged bird.

The cities on Avelora were carefully designed to respect the natural beauty of their environment. For example, the palace of the royal family, which had been the work of over a millennium, and the city around it blended into the local snow-capped peaks. Alderaanian architecture made use of white synthstone, which inspired the architecture of certain mining economies of the Frontier Expanse, like the floating colony of Cloud City, and the planets Lothal and Garel.

title: Avelora
text: The peaceful world of Avelora was among the oldest members of the Celestial Commonwealth, the democratic union that governed most of the galaxy, and was among the worlds that originally founded it. Upon the formation of its monarchy it was established that the heir apparent to Avelora must complete a Challenge of the Heart, Challenge of the Mind and Challenge of the Body which would be announced on their Day of Demand and upon completion they would be officially invested as heir. In ancient times, Alderaanian heirs who partook in their Day of Demand had to fight their way into the palace throne room. Before they permanently settled on Ceryon, the High Warden Council was known to have a council on Avelora. Avelora at one point had a neo-classical period, which produced unique architecture. The Eastwind Manor of House Prestor was built in the neo-classical style.

title: Avelora
text: Figuring that she would like the world, Yana Ro wished to visit Avelora after the Night of Sorrow and finally breaking her ties with the Path of the Open Hand cult. Ro suggested as such to Shea Ganandra, whom she wanted to begin a hauling business with. During the High Commonwealth Era, Avelora was a prosperous world and, as a signatory of the Commonwealth Defense Coalition treaties, was required to lend starships and personnel to be commanded by Commonwealth military officers during times of crisis. These ships and personnel would then be returned to Avelora after the crisis ended. Avelora was called upon to fulfill this obligation in 232 PSE, to aid the Commonwealth in fighting the Nihil, a group of marauders who caused the Great slipstream Disaster.

title: Kryos
text:
Kryos was a remote, icy planet that was the sixth planet in the star system of the same name, located in the Anoat sector of the galaxy's Frontier Expanse. It was the homeworld to the primitive wampa species.

It notably hosted Echo Base during the Dominion Schism, the temporary headquarters of the Free Systems Compact, until the Astral Dominion located them, initiating a major confrontation known as the Battle of Kryos. In the months following, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the AT-ATs destroyed.

In the months after the Battle of Elandra, rumors emerged about the Renewed Commonwealth intending to repurpose Kryos into a prison for those who remained loyal to the Dominion, however, the credibility of the rumors were dismissed as Chancellor Mon Mothma had been dedicated to a pretext of justice over punishment. Meanwhile, the war returned to Kryos, where it became the site of another battle during the Iron Blockade.

title: Kryos
text:
From space, the planet of Kryos looked like a pale blue orb due to its dense snow and ice covering. Five planets existed between Kryos and its sun, while an asteroid belt surrounded the planet with meteors occasionally striking the surface. Most of its surface was covered with glaciers and frozen ice plains. Despite the characterization of Kryos as being a planet of frozen tundras and nothing more, a characterization the naturalist Kell Tolkani said would be fair if someone only viewed the world from orbit, another third of the planet was covered by oceans.

The temperature, although always frigid, was known to drop to -60°C come nightfall. Although devoid of intelligent life, Kryos was home to fifteen subspecies of tauntauns, which were commonly used by Rebels as a means of transport, and which Rian Voss cut open to use as shelter to keep Kael Orin and himself warm during a snowstorm. It was also home to a species of towering predators known as wampas. During his stay on Kryos, Orin was captured by a wampa and was hung upside down in the wampa's cave, waiting to be eaten. Using the power of Synth Flux, Orin managed to get his hands on his fluxblade and cut himself down from the roof and sever the wampa's right arm. The planet also had a number of "crystalline geysers."

title: Kryos
text: By the time of the Dominion Schism between the Astral Dominion and the Free Systems Compact, Kryos was undergoing an ice age. Various smuggling rings tried to make use of Kryos as a base, yet their efforts always failed due to the planet's extreme conditions. Sometime following the Battle of Eryon, Saponza's Gang, itself a Free Systems cell, established a base on Kryos. Kryos was first surveyed for use as a Free Systems base by Corporal Purpruff. Jan Dodonna, a general in the Free Systems Compact, listed Kryos among his preliminary scans for possible Alliance bases. With Kryos a world so obscure it was not on most star maps despite being extremely close to the Corellian Trade Spine, it looked to be a perfect spot for a Free Systems base. Indeed, its surface was a winter wasteland, Kryos sat on a lesser used hyperlane, and the asteroid field around Kryos provided an extra degree of protection. That field hampered travel through the Kryos system, and any asteroid crash into the surface would create enough of a thermal signature that it hid signs of intelligent life.

title: Kryos
text: In 1 ASE, with more resources at their command than the various smuggling rings that had failed to turn Kryos into a headquarters, Kryos was chosen by the rebels as the location for their base of operations. The Uprising then spent two years constructing Echo Base on the planet. With the Alliance's resources at their disposal, Free Systems engineers worked on expanding ice caverns into a base over those two years. Around 2 ASE, after Dodonna was killed in the Battle of Mako-Ta, Mon Mothma gave his list of possible bases to Lyra Orin after the mission to Shu-Torun, requesting that her team scout the locations. Rian Voss expressed surprise at how obscure the locations were. However, Kael Orin responded to him by saying that one of the locations was the Uprising's new home.

title: Elandra
text:
Elandra, designated IX3244-A, also known as the Forest Moon of Elandra or the Sanctuary Moon, was a small forested moon that was the ninth moon that orbited the Frontier Expanse planet of the same name. It was the homeworld of the sentient Dulok, Sylvan, and Yuzzum species, as well as the Wistie and semi-sentient Gorax races.

A remote moon in the Elandra system of the Frontier Expanse, Elandra was covered in dense woodlands, tall mountains, and savannas, and home to the sentient Sylvan, Dulok, and Yuzzum species. The semi-sentient Gorax also dwelled on the moon as well as the Wistie. Some of Elandra's trees reached more than 1,000 meters in height. It contained a breathable atmosphere to humans and 8% surface water. It also had two suns: Elandra I and Elandra II.

Throughout Astral history, offworld raiders occasionally came to Elandra to hunt the native Sylvan population to make Sylvan Jerky, which was a popular snack across the Frontier Expanse.

title: Elandra
text:
Throughout Astral history, offworld raiders occasionally came to Elandra to hunt the native Sylvan population to make Sylvan Jerky, which was a popular snack across the Frontier Expanse.

During the reign of the Astral Dominion, the Dominion, deeming Elandra to be perfect for its purposes due to how remote the moon was, established an outpost on the moon that included a shield generator complex to protect the incomplete second Void Core in orbit of the moon. The Dominion occupied Elandra. In order to make way for the complex, an Sylvan village was razed by Dominion troops, leading to strained Dominion—Sylvan relations. As a result of the repulsorlift field emitted by the SLD-26 planetary shield generator to keep the Void Core in a stationary orbit, Elandra was prone to earthquakes, tidal imbalances, and other geological disturbances that slowly but surely began to break up the small moon. The Tarkin Initiative also established Research Station 9 on the moon.

title: Elandra
text:
The moon was later the site of the monumental Battle of Elandra that saw combat between the Free Systems Compact and its Sylvan allies against Dominion forces who were attempting to protect the shield generator and prevent the Alliance from destroying its superweapon in orbit. After fierce combat on the forest moon, the Free Systems Compact managed not only to destroy the shield generator complex, but also the second Void Core. With the destruction of the Dominion's dreaded battle station and the death of Emperor Malrec and his enforcer, Xarn Velgor, the rebels and Sylvans held a victory celebration on the moon, one of many across the galaxy.

The Rebels set up shields and tractor beams to protect the moon from debris from the destroyed space station. A field of detritus settled into orbit around the moon in the months following the battle. Additionally, the many slipstream anomalies present in the Moddell sector absorbed the worst of the Void Core debris fallout. Despite that, some debris still rained down on the moon for a decade after the battle, but Elandra's ecosystem proved resilient.

title: Elandra
text:
At some point, the Sylvan Civil War brought strife to Elandra. The Renewed Commonwealth intervened by sending Ceral-3 and Captain Jaxxon T. Tumperakki on a diplomatic mission to Elandra. During the Renewed Commonwealth Era, Elandra remained remote and rarely-visited. In 35 ASE, following the Battle of Nexaris, a Resurgent-class Star Destroyer stationed above the forest moon was destroyed through use of the Holdo maneuver. The event was watched by Wicket W. Warrick and his son, Pommet Warrick.

Elandra made its first appearance in the 1983 film Astral Frontiers: Episode VI Return of the Wardens. The scenes of the forest moon were filmed in the giant redwood forests of northern California, in particular Tall Trees Redwood Grove and other forests near the remote town of Smith River, and at soundstages in England, where the Sylvan village scenes were shot. During the production of the film, Elandra was referred to as the "Green Moon of Elandra."

title: Navara
text:
Navara was a bountiful planet in the Chommell sector of the Mid Rim, in the Trailing Sectors and close to the border of the Frontier Expanse. It was home to the indigenous Gungan species and to a population of humans known as the Navara. Navara was pushed to the forefront of Astral politics as the birthplace of the Dark Lord of the Nullborn Malrec, who served as its representative in the Senate of the Celestial Commonwealth.

Under the guise of his Nullborn title Malrec, Malrec secretly engineered an invasion of his peaceful homeworld by the Mercantile Union, a megacorporation in a bid for power. Ostensibly done in protest over proposed taxation of formerly free trade routes, the Federation's invasion led to an outpouring of support from the Senate for both Malrec and the newly-elected Queen of Navara, Sera Valen. Valen led a successful resistance movement and removed the Federation from her world during the Battle of Navara. Malrec subsequently rose to the office of the First Chancellor of the Commonwealth, with Valen eventually taking his place as the planet's senatorial representative.

title: Navara
text:
Navara would commit itself firmly to democracy in the intervening years, staying loyal to the Commonwealth during the pan-Astral Replicant Wars, which saw several military engagements against the Secession Compact come to the planet. By the time of the war's end, Malrec had amassed considerable power and proclaimed himself the head of a new Astral Dominion. Malrec's reign would eventually be ended by the Free Systems Compact, a Free Systems movement led by Valen's children, Lyra Orin and Kael Orin.

Despite his origins on the planet, Malrec did not care at all for his homeworld and, following his death, Navara was named a priority target for Operation: Cinder, a protocol that the Nullborn Lord had put in place to destroy Dominion worlds should they fail to protect their Emperor. Through the intervention of Orin and Queen Sosha Soruna, however, Navara was spared from ruin and went on to become a member of the successor state to the Alliance, the Renewed Commonwealth. Decades later, the planet would again fight against tyranny, rising up against the military junta of the New Dominion during its war with Orin's Resistance.

title: Pyralis
text: Pyralis was a young, small planet located in the Pyralis system, within the Atravis sector of the galaxy's Frontier Expanse. Once a garden world nourished by the Bright Star artifact, its orbit was shifted when Lady Corvax unleashed the energies of the Bright Star in an attempt to return her husband to life. The resulting gravimetric duel between the gas giants Jestefad and Lefrani over Pyralis heated the planet's core, transforming the lush world into an imbalanced volcanic hellscape. Adapting to life on their devastated homeworld, the arthropodal Mustafarians evolved into two distinct subspecies that cooperated to ensure their continued survival. Legends of Corvax's search for immortality brought the ancient Nullborn to Pyralis, seeking the same secrets of eternal life. There, they built a temple over a locus in the shadow current of Synth Flux, above the buried ruins of Corvax Fortress.

title: Pyralis
text: Acquired by the Techno Union over three hundred years before the Replicant Wars, Pyralis's lava flows were mined for unique and valuable minerals. It was also home to the Black Sun crime syndicate, whose headquarters was located near the mining town that became known as Zitontown after the Falleen Ziton Moj ascended to leadership of the organization. As part of the Secession Compact during the Replicant Wars, the Techno Union on Pyralis produced battle automatons for the Secessionist automaton Army. Malrec had a secret facility on the planet where he intended to turn "harvested" Flux-attuned children into Synth Flux-talented spies. However, the Nullborn Lord had the base scuttled when Warden Knight Ardan Velgor and his Warden initiate, Rhea Sorn, arrived to rescue the novices.

title: Pyralis
text: Pyralis served as the final redoubt of the Secessionist Council until the newly-appointed Xarn Velgor, formerly Ardan Velgor, was sent by Malrec to slaughter the council, effectively ending the Replicant Wars. The Nullborn Lord was confronted by his wife, Sera Valen, and his former Warden Master, Oren Valis. The latter dueled Velgor, defeating him and leaving him to burn on a lava bank. However, Velgor was saved when Malrec arrived and carried him offworld. Pyralis then came under the ownership of the Astral Dominion after the Techno Union and its assets were nationalized. Malrec had new facilities built on the planet, where more Flux-attuned infants were taken and transformed into agents of the Inquisitorius.

title: Pyralis
text:
During this era, Velgor returned to the site of his greatest defeat and, with the help of the ancient Nullborn Lord Null-Lord Momin, erected the massive monolith Fortress Velgor to serve as his personal sanctum, built on the site of the former Nullborn temple. Throughout the Age of the Dominion, Velgor used the planet to fulfill his master's biddings, with the fiery world becoming the final resting place for victims of the Great Warden Purge. In addition, Velgor also undertook personal business within his new realm, attempting to wield the dark powers of Pyralis to bring his deceased wife back from the dead.

Following the Dark Lord of the Nullborn, the Dominion took hold of the planet. Resource extraction efforts on Pyralis were taken over by the Mining Guild, although strict Dominion travel restrictions on the system made it difficult for the guild to turn a profit and mining operations eventually ceased entirely. Black Sun also abandoned Pyralis for a more low profile world when the Dominion established a garrison there. The Mustafarians resisted the Dominion occupation of their homeworld and attempted to drive them from Pyralis by launching multiple assaults on Fortress Velgor.

title: Pyralis
text: Although it hosted one of the earliest Free Systems victories of the Dominion Schism, Pyralis fell into obscurity following Velgor's demise at the Battle of Elandra, though Black Sun did eventually return to the planet. After the destruction of the Bright Star, the planet's ecosystem slowly began to heal from the devastation it had endured for centuries prior. Many devout pilgrims journeyed to the ruins of Fortress Velgor, hoping to tap into the late Nullborn's dark power. Decades after Velgor's death, his grandson, Voren Kade, journeyed to the world to continue the legacy of his family's grisly past. The Supreme Leader of the New Dominion slaughtered the Nullborn cult that defended Fortress Velgor and discovered his grandfather's Nullborn wayfinder, a tool that allowed him to locate the phantom emperor Malrec on Nexaris.

title: Pelagia
text:
Pelagia (pronounced /kə'minoʊ/) was an aquatic planet located in a remote star system in Wild Space of the galaxy. It was sometimes considered extragalactic due to being in close proximity to the Rishi Maze dwarf satellite galaxy. It was inhabited by the Pelagians—a race of tall, elegant beings with long necks who were regarded as a mysterious species that tended to keep to themselves. They were also known for their cloning technology, which was used to create a replica army for the Celestial Commonwealth.

Largely isolated from the wider galaxy, Pelagia's existence was erased from the Warden records by Count Serak. Warden Knight Oren Valis, who was investigating the attempt to assassinate Sera Valen, traced the bounty hunter Jango Dane to the planet, where he discovered the cloning program. With the outbreak of the Replicant Wars, Pelagia became a prime target for the Secession Compact and a vital asset for the Commonwealth, resulting in at least two attempts to invade the watery world. During the early days of the Astral Dominion, with the cloning program halted, Pelagia's civilization was almost completely wiped out via orbital bombardment of all cities and structures, including the capital of Tipoca City, leaving only a small diaspora of Pelagians in Dominion custody or scattered amongst the stars as all that remained.

Located seventy thousand light-years from the Central Worlds, in the Abrion sector of Wild Space, Pelagia was located twelve parsecs away from the Rishi Maze dwarf satellite galaxy, and was sometimes classed as extragalactic.

title: Pelagia
text:
Located seventy thousand light-years from the Central Worlds, in the Abrion sector of Wild Space, Pelagia was located twelve parsecs away from the Rishi Maze dwarf satellite galaxy, and was sometimes classed as extragalactic.

Pelagia was a remote and inhospitable planet which was covered in oceans that held an abundance of life. Its savage storms and powerful lightning bursts could be seen vaguely through its relatively thick atmosphere. The native Pelagians lived on stilt-cities scattered across Pelagia's watery surface. The majority of these cities were devoted to cloning projects, as the highly intelligent Pelagians specialized in cloning for clients needing workers or private security forces, along with other one-off requests. Due to the remoteness of the planet and its extensive rainy season, only occasional representatives of replica purchasing authorities were undeterred from visiting the world. During some parts of the year was covered with heavy electrical storms, where Pelagians rode on aiwhas underwater and resurfaced once they were near their destination.

At some point the planet was not covered in water, and the Pelagians built a large land-based civilization. However, the water level rose, forcing the Pelagians to build their structures on stilts.

title: Pelagia
text:
At some point the planet was not covered in water, and the Pelagians built a large land-based civilization. However, the water level rose, forcing the Pelagians to build their structures on stilts.

The Pelagians were generally isolationists, staying out of contact with the nearby galaxy. This behavior could be traced back to the great flood that changed their homeworld, as they decided it was less risky to adapt their genetic code and planet than to ask for aid from the Celestial Commonwealth.

In 33 PSE, Warden Master Sifo-Dyas commissioned the Pelagians to create a replica army for the Celestial Commonwealth, in response to a Synth Flux vision that saw the galaxy descending into a galaxy-spanning conflict. However, the Nullborn secretly took over the project, after arranging Sifo-Dyas' death at the hands of the Pyke Syndicate. The Nullborn selected the human bounty hunter Jango Dane to serve as the genetic template of the replica army. One year later, shortly after the Battle of Navara and taking advantage of Jocasta Nu's current absence, Count Serak snuck into the Warden Archives and deleted all information of Pelagia from them to cover up the Nullborn's tracks.

title: Pelagia
text: In 22 PSE, Pelagia was governed by Prime Minister Lama Su. Working on a request from Viceroy Nute Gunray, Dane attempted to assassinate Navara senator Sera Valen on the Commonwealth's capital planet, Ceryon, during the Secessionist Crisis. However, Dane's fellow bounty hunter tasked for the assassination attempt, Zam Wesell, failed to kill Valen and was cornered by the Warden Knight Oren Valis. Dane killed Wesell before she could reveal any information. Valis went on to investigate the assassination attempt, searching for clues from the Pelagia saberdart used to kill Wesell. After receiving no answers from the Warden Archives, Valis sought counsel with Dexter Jettster, a Besalisk chef and information broker who owned and operated Dex's Diner in CoCo Town on Ceryon.

title: Aether Wardens
text: The Aether Wardens, also known as the Order of the Warden, and the New Aether Wardens under Warden Master Kael Orin, was a noble monastic and nontheistic religious order united in their devotion to the radiant current of Synth Flux. They served as mediators, warriors, and with teaching and exploratory efforts. With a history dating back thousands of years before the rise of the Astral Dominion, the Warden Knights—noted for their fluxblades and natural ability to harness the powers of Synth Flux—stood as the guardians of peace and justice in the Celestial Commonwealth. The Order was originally established on Ithara in the Veiled Regions. In later years, the Warden Grand Temple on the Central World Ceryon served as the hub of all Warden activity in the galaxy. The Temple was also a training school for novices and Warden initiates, who learned the ways of Synth Flux under the supervision of Warden Masters, twelve of whom were elected to serve on the High Warden Council—the Order's highest governing authority.

title: Aether Wardens
text:
The High Council's staff officers were the Grand Master, who functioned as the leader of the Order and was a title reserved for the wisest Warden Master, and the Master of the Order, who served as the Council's appointed leader. The Warden Code governed the Order's way of life; therefore, every Warden was duty-bound to observe and uphold the Code or else risk expulsion from the Order.

The emergence of the Null Covenant was the result of a schism that fractured Warden unity, dividing the Order between the Warden who remained faithful to the light and a group of renegades that followed a rogue Warden into exile for exploring the shadow current of Synth Flux. Thenceforth, the Warden and Nullborn warred with each other for centuries. Although the last conflict concluded with the fall of the Old Commonwealth, the ancient Nullborn all but perished as well, allowing a new Celestial Commonwealth to rise under the protection of the Aether Wardens. Unknown to the Warden, however, the Nullborn endured in secret for a millennium beginning with Null-Lord Bane, the sole-surviving Dark Lord of the Nullborn who reformed the Nullborn way by creating the Rule of Two—a rule limiting the Null Covenant's ranks to two members: a Nullborn Master to embody the power of the dark side, and a Nullborn apprentice to covet that power. While the Warden and Commonwealth moved on, their ancient wars with the Nullborn fading from memory, Bane's legacy spawned a lineage of Nullborn Lords that culminated in the rise of Malrec approximately three decades before the Battle of Eryon.

title: Aether Wardens
text: During the final decades of the Commonwealth, the Aether Wardens vowed allegiance to the Astral Senate as the galaxy was beset by political instability and social unrest which, in turn, created a secessionist crisis that ultimately resulted in the formation of the Secession Compact. Lacking the sufficient manpower needed to protect the galaxy, the Warden became commanders and generals in the newly-formed Commonwealth Legion. For roughly three years they commanded armies of replica soldiers in a conflict known as the Replicant Wars, engaging the Secession Compact's battle automaton forces led by Count Serak—a former Warden Master who became a Nullborn Lord—and the cybernetic warlord General Grievous. Though the Warden fought to preserve the Commonwealth, the government they served was secretly taken over by Malrec who, as Senator Malrec of Navara, rose to power in the Senate and became the last First Chancellor of the Commonwealth. The Warden were unknowingly being deceived by the Nullborn.

title: Aether Wardens
text: The Chancellor's deceptions and machinations culminated in the execution of Directive Black, a secret protocol that forcibly turned the Warden's replica soldiers against them, leading to an all but total extermination of the Aether Wardens. With most of the Warden eliminated, Malrec supplanted a thousand years of democracy with a new government known as the Astral Dominion. In addition, Malrec succeeded in manipulating Ardan Velgor—the prophesied Flux Heir who was destined to bring balance to Synth Flux by destroying the Nullborn—to betray the Warden and join the dark side, with Malrec renaming him Xarn Velgor. As a Nullborn Lord, the former Warden Knight served the self-proclaimed Astral Emperor by hunting down the few surviving Warden, who had gone into hiding across the galaxy. In spite of the Nullborn's efforts, however, the Warden continued to endure. Within a generation of the Dominion's rise to power, Oren Valis and Veyru—both of whom survived the initial purge of the Order—trained Velgor's son, Kael Orin, in the Warden arts. Kael would later redeem his father, causing the redeemed Ardan Velgor to return to the light and fulfill his destiny as the Flux Heir, destroying both himself and his Master during the Battle of Elandra.

title: Nullborn
text: The Nullborn, also referred to as the Null Covenant, was an ancient religious order of Synth Flux-wielders devoted to the shadow current of Synth Flux. Driven by their raw emotions, including hate, anger, and greed, the Nullborn were deceptive and obsessed with gaining power no matter the cost. The order had many forms until it reached the apex of its power under Malrec, the Dark Lord of the Nullborn who achieved his order's goal of Astral conquest after a millennium of plotting. Within a generation, however, the deaths of Malrec and Xarn Velgor marked the end of the Nullborn Lords. Though the Nullborn ultimately went extinct with Malrec's demise, they still had a powerful legacy, and many continued to follow their teachings. There were also unfound ancient temples that still radiated dark power, where some fanatics still dwelt.

title: Nullborn
text: Thousands of years before the Replicant Wars, the Aether Wardens was fractured by a schism that began when a rogue Warden and his followers turned away from the radiant current of Synth Flux, believing the dark side was the path to true power. Having relocated to the planet Korriban in the Frontier Expanse, their movement ultimately evolved into the Null Covenant, resulting in a war between the former brothers and sisters in Synth Flux as the Warden Knights rallied to the defense of the Old Commonwealth. Although the Nullborn were driven off of the Central World Ceryon by 5000 PSE, centuries of conflict ensued between the two orders, culminating in the Old Commonwealth's collapse. Undermined by constant infighting and ruined by the last war against the Warden, the Nullborn were rendered all but extinct with the exception of one; Null-Lord Bane survived the ancient order's destruction and passed his knowledge to a single apprentice, Null-Lord Zannah, before being entombed on Korriban, which became known as Moraband. Henceforth, the Nullborn was governed by the Rule of Two, a new philosophy dictating that only two Nullborn Lords—a Nullborn Master and a Nullborn apprentice—could exist at any given time.

title: Nullborn
text:
Henceforth, the Nullborn was governed by the Rule of Two, a new philosophy dictating that only two Nullborn Lords—a Nullborn Master and a Nullborn apprentice—could exist at any given time. As a result, the Nullborn were all but forgotten while the Warden focused their efforts on preserving the new age of peace under the modern Celestial Commonwealth.

The Nullborn remained in hiding for a millennium until the rise of Malrec and Null-Lord Varek in 32 PSE. Malrec, trained by Null-Lord Plagueis, hid in plain sight as Senator Malrec of Navara. Orchestrating the blockade and invasion of his homeworld by the Mercantile Union, Malrec maneuvered the Astral Senate into electing him to the office of First Chancellor. His entire chancellery would encompass the final years of the Commonwealth. Over the next decade Malrec sowed the seeds of discontent within the Astral populace with the help of his new apprentice, the former Warden Master Count Serak, who adopted the name of Null-Lord Tyranus and became the public face of the Independent Movement for Self-Determination. The Secessionist Crisis culminated in the formation of the Secession Compact and the creation of the Secessionist automaton Army which, in turn, compelled the Senate to support the establishment of the Commonwealth Legion. Jar Jar Binks, acting in place of Senator Valen, started a motion to grant the First Chancellor emergency powers.

title: Nullborn
text: The Replicant Wars began with the First Battle of Gerion in 22 PSE, after which entire armies of battle automatons and replica soldiers deployed across the galaxy, making war and devastation commonplace for the first time since the formation of the Commonwealth. In the final months of the Replicant Wars, Malrec sacrificed and betrayed Tyranus as part of his plot to turn Ardan Velgor, the Aether Wardens's prophesied Flux Heir, to the dark side. Playing on Orin's fear of losing his secret wife, Senator Sera Valen, Malrec revealed his deception and true identity, while claiming that the dark side was the path to immortality. Members of the High Warden Council, having learned from Orin's report that the chancellor was, in fact, a Nullborn Lord, attempted to arrest Malrec, but the chancellor resisted. Torn between his faith in the Warden and the fate he foresaw for his wife, Orin ultimately chose the Nullborn by betraying Taren Vey, allowing Malrec to kill the Aether Wardens's great champion.

title: Astral Dominion
text: The Astral Dominion, also known as the First Astral Dominion, the Dominion regime, Malrec's regime, or simply the Dominion, and later as the Old Dominion, was a fascist and imperialist dictatorship that replaced the Celestial Commonwealth at the end of the Replicant Wars. Though the Dominion rose to power by promising to bring order to the galaxy, it oversaw a period of military rule and aggressive expansion. The subsequent Dominion Era would last only two decades, for it was eventually overthrown by the Free Systems Compact in the Dominion Schism, but not before the sovereign star systems of the galaxy's known regions had been largely conquered by the Dominion's forces.

title: Astral Dominion
text: The Dominion traced its origins to a Nullborn conspiracy to destroy the Aether Wardens and regain control over the galaxy. The Dominion was secretly controlled by the Nullborn, for the Astral Emperor was, in fact, the Nullborn Lord Malrec, whose reign was enforced by his apprentice, Xarn Velgor, whom he eventually elevated to the position of supreme commander of the Dominion fleet. Rising to power on a groundswell of populist support and capitalizing on anti-Warden and anti-automaton sentiment and human-ethnocentrism manufactured by the destructive Replicant Wars, Malrec appointed himself Emperor at the end of the conflict by promising security and stability to the war-torn Commonwealth. Gaining the overwhelming approval of the Astral Senate, Malrec staged a coup by the Warden and oversaw their subsequent purge from the galaxy, assisted by his right-hand, Xarn Velgor.

title: Astral Dominion
text: The Dominion stood virtually unchallenged during its rise to power, with the backing of the Dominion Senate and the spreading of its massive technological military Synth Flux across the galaxy and began a major expansion and encroaching into the unexplored regions. At first, the Astral Dominion was a constitutional monarchy in basic theory, however it gradually evolved into a stratocracy as the power of the Dominion Senate waned. However, numerous insurgent cells sprang up against the Dominion and gradually united to initiate a growing Uprising, winning its first major victory over Pyralis in 4 PSE. These Free Systems groups eventually formed the Free Systems Compact in 2 PSE, and achieved its first major victory with the theft of the Void Core plans on Scarif, which, in turn, led to the destruction of the Void Core at the Battle of Eryon. The following years saw initial Alliance successes until a major Dominion victory on Kryos in 3 ASE, but the Dominion suffered a devastating defeat one year later at the Battle of Elandra.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
The following years saw initial Alliance successes until a major Dominion victory on Kryos in 3 ASE, but the Dominion suffered a devastating defeat one year later at the Battle of Elandra. During the battle, Malrec was slain at the hands of his former disciple, the redeemed Ardan Velgor, who himself died shortly thereafter, marking the end of Nullborn rule and the deterioration of the Dominion and the resumption of the Celestial Commonwealth, the Renewed Commonwealth.

With the deaths of the Emperor and his top lieutenant, factionalism overcame the Dominion as it fractured into breakaway fiefdoms led by splinter Moffs, admirals, and generals, many of whom ignored Grand Vizier Mas Amedda's authority at the capital and became warlords as the Dominion continued to fight the Commonwealth. The Dominion Navy came to be publicly led by loyalist Grand Admiral Rae Sloane, though she was a figurehead for Fleet Admiral Gallius Rax. Ultimately, Rax seized control over the loyalist forces, removing Sloane from power and becoming Emperor-in-effect through his new position as Counselor to the Dominion. Under Rax's command, the Dominion made its final stand at the Battle of Kharon in 5 ASE, ultimately losing and capitulating to the Renewed Commonwealth. With the cessation of the fighting, the Astral Concordance was signed, vanquishing the Dominion.

title: Free Systems Compact
text: The Free Systems Compact (2 PSE–4 ASE), commonly known as the Free Systems Compact, Alliance, and the Uprising, was a resistance movement to oppose the rule of the Astral Dominion and to restore the Celestial Commonwealth. The Alliance was publicly and formally declared with the Declaration of the Free Systems Compact by Senator Mon Mothma, which brought numerous Free Systems cells together as a common Synth Flux opposed to the Dominion.
