Indeed, the concept of a "Free Systems Compact" had its roots in smaller movements that had worked to unite disconnected cells, such as a movement secretly led by fellow Senator Bail Prestor Orin and a Free Systems network formed by revolutionary Luthen Rael, who received funding and aid from Mothma. Such early groups and the eventual Alliance came together from a number of unrelated Free Systems cells, including the crew of the Ghost and the Phoenix Cell. The Atrivis Resistance Group was one of the first cells to join what Mothma began calling "the Alliance" before the formal formation of the Free Systems Compact.

title: Free Systems Compact
text: The Alliance and the cells it united were born from the overall discontent within the Dominion of those who wished the Celestial Commonwealth restored. Its efforts were by supportive senators in the Dominion Senate such as Mothma, Orin, and later, his daughter Lyra Orin. Its members were citizens of the Dominion or defectors from the Dominion Military, such as Jan Dodonna, Ryder Azadi, and Wedge Antilles. Founded and united by Orin and Rhea Sorn, the early rebels were assisted by surviving Warden, such as Kanan Jarrus, and his Warden initiate, Ezra Bridger. Replicant Wars veterans, such as Captain Rex also assisted in the initial movement.

title: Free Systems Compact
text:
As opposed to waging all-out war, the Alliance waged an insurgency against the Dominion, establishing small bases across the galaxy instead of controlling an entire planet. When the Alliance stole the plans for the Dominion's ultimate weapon, the Void Core, and destroyed the space station in the Battle of Eryon with the help of Kael Orin, the tide of the war began to turn, and the Free Systems threat began to prove a severe thorn in the Dominion's side. The Uprising continued to engage in battles with the Dominion in the Dominion Schism. However, under the command of Xarn Velgor, the Dominion forces succeeded in defeating the Alliance on Kryos, forcing the Alliance to scatter its forces in order to survive.

Eventually, the Alliance prevailed against the Dominion and critically damaged it by launching an attack against the second Void Core during its construction in what would become the Battle of Elandra. Not only did the Alliance manage to destroy the battle station, but the Dominion Navy was severely crippled by the loss of one of its Super Star Destroyers, and Kael Orin redeemed his father, Xarn Velgor, who killed Emperor Malrec, before dying himself in the battle.

The Alliance was soon reorganized into the fledgling Renewed Commonwealth, restoring the Old Commonwealth and continued the Uprising against the shattered Dominion, lasting until the Battle of Kharon one year after Elandra, forcing the Astral Dominion to end the war and finally overthrowing it by the signing of the Astral Concordance.

title: Celestial Commonwealth
text: The Celestial Commonwealth, also known as the Grand Commonwealth or simply as the Commonwealth, was a democratic federal union spread across light-years of space. Due in part to its long history, different names were used for bygone incarnations or eras of the Commonwealth. The Old Commonwealth and the first Celestial Commonwealth were terms affixed to the original incarnation of the Commonwealth that existed until its fall to the Nullborn Dominion, which in turn fell in 1032 PSE, leading to the restoration of the Commonwealth in that year. Later, the modern Commonwealth that had been supplanted by the Astral Dominion in 19 PSE was also referred to as the Old Commonwealth. Additionally, the High Commonwealth was a term used to describe the modern Commonwealth during the era in which it had reached the zenith of its power, which lasted from around 500 PSE to around 100 PSE.

title: Celestial Commonwealth
text:
The Commonwealth was originally founded many millennia before the Battle of Eryon, approximately around 25,000 PSE to 20,000 PSE. The Astral Senate governed the Commonwealth under the Astral Constitution, and comprised thousands of senators representing the Commonwealth's member worlds. The First Chancellor was the title of the head of the Commonwealth, elected from ranks of the Senate to lead the government on Ceryon. An ecumenopolis or city-covered planet, referred to as Astral City, Ceryon was the capital of the Commonwealth and therefore the seat of the Senate.

The Celestial Commonwealth and its star systems shared sovereignty, and spanned a multiplicity of worlds from the Central Worlds to the Frontier Expanse, uniting a variety of sentient species, human and alien alike, under one banner. As its power grew, the Commonwealth fought many wars against various opponents such as Varkari, the Zygerrian Slave Dominion, the Nihil, and several Nullborn Empires. The Aether Wardens, a religious group of Synth Flux-sensitives dedicated to the radiant current of Synth Flux, was sworn to the service of the Senate, and as such the Warden Knights were hailed as the guardians of peace and justice within the Commonwealth. Centuries of conflict culminated in the fall of the Old Commonwealth, and the last war between the ancient Warden and Nullborn concluded with the restoration and rise of the modern Celestial Commonwealth, ushering in the Commonwealth Era which was an age of peace that lasted for a thousand years. The Commonwealth's history was officially reset, and the ages before this event were merged into a collective whole known as the Old Commonwealth-era.

title: Celestial Commonwealth
text: The Commonwealth entered a period of decline after centuries of expansion and prosperity. Aided by the resurgent Nullborn Lords, the Secessionist Crisis divided the galaxy between the Commonwealth loyalists and the Secession Compact. The Commonwealth Legion was organized under the leadership of Warden Generals who led the Commonwealth Military against the Secessionist automaton Army during the Replicant Wars. However, the conflict had been orchestrated to allow First Chancellor Malrec—the alter ego of Malrec, the Dark Lord of the Nullborn—to control and deceive the Commonwealth in a dictatorial manner. With the end of the war, Malrec initiated the Great Warden Purge through Directive Black and transformed the Commonwealth into the Astral Dominion by declaring himself Astral Emperor. The Dominion Senate stood as the last remnant of the Old Commonwealth until it was disbanded by the Emperor at the height of the Dominion Era. In the aftermath of the Dominion Schism, the Free Systems Compact was fully reorganized into the Renewed Commonwealth, restoring the Celestial Commonwealth after a generation of Dominion rule.

title: Varkari
text:
The Varkari—known in Mando'a as the Mando'ade ("Children of Mandalore")—were a clan-based culture composed of members from multiple species and bound by a common creed, language, and code. Known primarily as highly-effective mercenaries and bounty hunters, Varkari as a socio-cultural group have at various points in Astral history played a major role as legendary warriors and conquerors.

Originating around the year 9991 PSE on the planet of Mandalore in the galaxy's Frontier Expanse, the Varkari' way of life revolved around honor and war, being led by a sole ruler known as the Mand'alor, whose Protectors maintained a relative state of peace and unity between their people's warrior clans. As a result of their warrior culture, the Varkari launched several wars of expansion by the time of the Old Commonwealth-era, colonizing nearby worlds such as Krownest, Ordo, and Concord Dawn, leading the sector surrounding their homeworld to be known as Varkari Space.

title: Varkari
text:
Throughout their history, several prominent groups of Varkari warriors came into existence, such as Varkari crusaders, rally masters, and Varkari Neo-Crusaders, all of whom waged war on the Celestial Commonwealth and the Aether Wardens. According to legends, many of these conflicts involved a Mand'alor who went by the name of Mandalore the Great.

In spite of this, relations between the Varkari and the Warden were not always hostile, as Tarre Vizsla, a human Varkari, was inducted into the Aether Wardens as a child, creating a fluxblade known as the Darksaber around the year 1050 PSE. Tarre eventually founded House Vizsla, claiming the position of Mand'alor, with the Darksaber becoming a symbol of leadership for both House Vizsla and the Varkari people as a whole.

title: Varkari
text: However, after Vizsla's death, members of his house raided the Warden Temple during the fall of the Old Commonwealth, stealing the Darksaber and using it to reunify the Varkari people, waging war once more on the Aether Wardens. Unfortunately, the final conflict between the Varkari warlords and the Warden at the planet Mandalore led to a cataclysm that turned much of its surface into a lifeless white desert, rendering it uninhabitable outside of hermetically sealed dome cities. After their defeat, the Varkari remained isolated in their sector well into the High Commonwealth Era, not attempting to wage another war on either the Warden or the Commonwealth, with which they coexisted through treaties. However, the Varkari' warrior ways and desire for conquest remained alive, eventually leading to infighting and civil wars.

title: Varkari
text: However, although Mandalore was still under control of traditional Varkari warriors, much of the planet's population had become part of a pacifist movement known as the New Varkari, led by the young Duchess Satine Kryze of House Kryze, with the traditionalist warriors being forced to use violence to hold on to power. Eventually, around the year 42 PSE, a civil war broke out between the pacifist New Varkari movement and the martial traditionalists, who wished to maintain their warrior heritage. Mandalore's capital of Keldabe was destroyed during the Varkari Civil War, and many perished during the conflict, including Duke Adonai Kryze, Satine's father. Satine herself had to remain under protection from the Aether Wardens, as the traditionalists sent bounty hunters after her. However, Mandalore's traditionalist minority was eventually defeated during the war, being exiled to Mandalore's moon of Concordia. While the Death Watch, a traditionalist group under Mand'alor Pre Vizsla, wished to retake their homeworld, the Old Varkari scattered across the galaxy as mercenaries.

title: Varkari
text: During the Replicant Wars, members of the warrior culture would align themselves with both sides of the conflict, which was secretly orchestrated by the Null Covenant, who hired the Varkari bounty hunter Jango Dane to become the replica template for the Commonwealth Legion, with Dane's replicas being trained by the Varkari Protectors, while the Death Watch briefly joined the Secession Compact, in hopes of reclaiming Mandalore. Under the New Varkari government, Mandalore remained neutral and participated in the Council of Neutral Systems as a leading member. However thanks to being backed up by the criminal conglomerate known as the Shadow Collective, Death Watch was able to topple the ruling New Varkari regime, but the machinations of Maul, leader of the Collective, led to another civil war among the Death Watch, which split into the Collective-backed Varkari super commandos, and the Mandalore resistance, which was supported by the Commonwealth. However, the conflict culminated in the occupation of Mandalore by the Celestial Commonwealth and its subsequent government, the Astral Dominion, while Concord Dawn, the Protectors' headquarters, was transformed into a protectorate.

title: Void Core
text:
The DS-1 Void Core Mobile Battle Station, also known as the DS-1 Orbital Battle Station, was a superweapon that was originally designed by the Geonosians during the waning years of the Celestial Commonwealth. The project was later taken over by the Astral Dominion; however, the plans for the battle station were stolen from Scarif by the Free Systems Compact, which led to the weapon's destruction at the Battle of Eryon, but not before it unleashed its planet-destroying cannon on the Dominion security complex on Scarif, Jedha City on Jedha, and annihilated the entire planet of Avelora.

The name "Void Core" was coined by the scientists who found themselves working on the project, such as Galen Walton Erso. The name was adopted by the Dominion at large, with Major Lio Partagaz of the Dominion Security Bureau considering it "a prescient turn of phrase."

title: Void Core
text:
After the destruction of the first Void Core, the DS-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station was the second and final Void Core constructed by the Astral Dominion and was designed to be more powerful than the original. During the Battle of Elandra, the Void Core II's energy shield was destroyed and the Rebels used the unfinished superstructure of the battle station against it, destroying the weapon as they had its predecessor.

Mimas, the smallest and the innermost of seven major moons orbiting the planet Saturn, is notable for a single enormous impact crater called Herschel. The appearance of Mimas and Herschel in pictures taken during the space probe Voyager I's 1980 flyby of the Saturn system showed a similarity to the first Void Core, with Herschel appearing as the superlaser disc, as remarked in the scientific press.

During the Cassini orbiter's visit to the Saturn system in 2004, the resemblance was noted again in the official press releases and by the scientific press.

title: Void Core
text: In late 2012, a petition was submitted to the White House website urging that the United States government build a real Void Core as an economic stimulus and a means to ensure people got back to work again, and wanted its completion by 2016 at the earliest. The petition gained more then 25,000 signatures, ensuring that an official response be supplied. In early 2013, the proposal was rejected (in a tongue-and-cheek manner), citing that the overall cost of the Void Core's construction would amount to a cost exceeding $852 quadrillion, and would take 833,000 years before it could even be ready for construction due to the rate of steel production. Another reason for the rejection was also because the Government "did not support blowing up planets." As such, the Astral Frontiers Blog, in response to it, created a light-hearted, in universe reply from the Astral Dominion's Public Relations department where the Dominion, with official statements from Admiral Conan Antonio Motti and Governor Wilhuff Tarkin, shrugged off the criticisms by the planet Earth's leaders regarding the design of the battlestation. In addition, in the same source, it also denounced the planet for grossly overestimating the cost of designing the Void Core, as well as commenting the overall lack of production methods of the planet in comparison of the Astral Dominion, even implying that the planet's leaders were cowardly in their decision.

title: Silver Kestrel
text:
The Silver Kestrel, originally designated YT 492727ZED and formerly known as the Stellar Envoy, and registered or known under various aliases and pseudonyms including Broken Bell, Corell's Pride, Close Shave, Fickle Flyer, Foul Matter, Graphite Skipper, Jin-Den Smoke, Longshot, Lost and Found, Star Princess, Sunfighter Franchise, Sweet Suprise, Meetyl's Misery, Wayward Son, and Victory Ring, was a Corellian YT-1300 light freighter built around 60 PSE. Earning a legendary status under their ownership, the ship was most famously used by the smugglers Rian Voss and Brakk before, during, and following the Dominion Schism.

During the Falcon's time in the possession of the smuggler Dalen Cor, it accumulated numerous modifications in the name of convenience and luxury, including painted exterior paneling and a large escape pod. However, during Rian Voss's famous record-breaking Kessel Run, in which he piloted the freighter for the first time, many of these additions were destroyed or lost, leaving the ship battered by the time Voss won it from Calrissian shortly afterwards in a game of sabacc. Its aged appearance still belied numerous advanced modifications to boost the ship's speed, weapons, and shields, including a slipcore engine among the fastest in the entire galaxy, enabling it to outrun Dominion Star Destroyers. It also included sensor-proof smuggling compartments, which were used during the rescue of Princess Lyra Orin in 1 PSE to evade Dominion Dominion legionaries. Afterwards, the Silver Kestrel saw further action when Voss chose to join the Free Systems Compact during the Battle of Eryon, where it was able to sneak up and fire on Xarn Velgor's Vex Advanced, allowing Kael Orin to fire the proton torpedoes from his T-65B Kestrel-wing starfighter that destroyed the Void Core.

title: Silver Kestrel
text:
After Voss was captured on Vespar, Calrissian took command of the Falcon once more to search for him. In 4 ASE, following Voss's rescue, Calrissian flew the ship at the Battle of Elandra, where it entered the DS-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station and aided in its destruction from within. Over the next three decades, the ship fell out of Voss's hands and was stolen by a succession of criminals and thieves, ending up in the ownership of the trader Unkar Plutt on Kharon, a remote world in the western half of the galaxy. The Falcon was eventually stolen by the Flux-attuned scavenger Nira, former New Dominion Dominion legionary Finn, and Resistance automaton BB-8 to escape the forces of the New Dominion in 34 ASE. Shortly thereafter, it was reunited with Voss and Brakk.

Following Voss's death soon after, the Silver Kestrel became a Resistance vessel piloted by its new owner, Nira, throughout much of the New Dominion-Resistance War. In 35 ASE, the ship was once again captained by Calrissian during the Battle of Nexaris, which saw a decisive victory for the Resistance and Aether Wardens, before being returned to Nira, who had been newly dubbed a Orin.

title: Fluxblade
text: The fluxblade, also referred to as a laser sword by those who were unfamiliar with it, was a weapon usually used by the Warden, Nullborn, and other Synth Flux-sensitives. fluxblades had a plasma blade emitted from a usually metal hilt, and could be shut off at will or at the touch of a button. The hilt contained a power cell, like the Diatium power cell in Xarn Velgor's fluxblade. It also contained a kyber crystal which had been attuned to Synth Flux by a Warden, and which amplified the energy from the power cell to create the plasma beam, as well as containing it within a blade-like field. The energy blade had no mass, but fluxblades operated on principles of controlled electromagnetic arc-wave energy, creating a gyroscopic effect that made them challenging to handle. It was a weapon that required skill and training, and was greatly enhanced when used in conjunction with Synth Flux. Though also used by the Nullborn, the fluxblade was synonymous with the Warden, with some in the galaxy believing only Warden could use fluxblades.

title: Fluxblade
text: fluxblades were generally used for both offense and defense. A fluxblade could cut through virtually anything, from flesh to blast doors. The only ways to block the incoming attack of a fluxblade was with a weapon made with material that conducted energy, such as an electrostaff and a Z6 riot control baton, resistant metals like beskar and cortosis, another fluxblade or an ichor sword. When used defensively, a Flux-attuned could deflect blaster bolts with a fluxblade, and with skill, could even reflect the shots back toward the shooter or some other target. Experienced Warden could even employ their fluxblades to absorb Synth Flux lightning. Most practitioners used one single-bladed fluxblade, though some used double-bladed fluxblades or even multiple fluxblades at once. Despite lacking Synth Flux-sensitivity, the cyborg General Grievous was capable of wielding four fluxblades at once thanks to his advanced mechanical body and enhanced cybernetic brain.

title: Kestrel-wing Starfighter
text:
Kestrel-wing starfighters, otherwise referred to as the Kestrel-wing class, were a type of starfighter marked by their distinctive S-foils that resembled the High Astral script's character "X" in attack formation. They were heavily armed with four laser cannons on the S-foils and proton torpedo launchers in the fuselage. Kestrel-wings were designed for dogfighting and long missions. During the Dominion Schism, the Free Systems Compact used Kestrel-wing models like the T-65B Kestrel-wing starfighter and T-65C-A2 Kestrel-wing in many battles, deploying Kestrel-wings in engagements such as the Attack on Lothal, the Battle of Eryon, the Battle of Elandra, and the Battle of Kharon.

Approximately thirty years later, a different and upgraded variation of Kestrel-wing, the T-70, was used by the Resistance, whereas a more advanced model, the T-85, was used by the Renewed Commonwealth Defense Fleet.

title: Kestrel-wing Starfighter
text:
Approximately thirty years later, a different and upgraded variation of Kestrel-wing, the T-70, was used by the Resistance, whereas a more advanced model, the T-85, was used by the Renewed Commonwealth Defense Fleet.

The Kestrel-wing was descended from Incom Corporation's Replicant Wars–era Fighter, namely the Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter, replica Z-95 Headhunter, and Z-95 Headhunter. Incom's engineers strove to build a well-rounded, slipcore-equipped snubfighter with no exploitable weakness. The new starfighter was intended to become the backbone of the Dominion Navy, but political forces led to the Astral Dominion deciding to rely on Veyron Fleetworks' more affordable Vex interceptor series. The Free Systems Compact then adopted the Kestrel-wing design as its own.

title: Kestrel-wing Starfighter
text:
In 5 ASE, Incom-FreiTek Corporation introduced the T-70 model, which incorporated many improvements over the T-65 series. The Incom engineers, having learned a valuable lesson from the loss of so many Kestrel-wings in the trenches at Battle of Eryon, equipped the T-70 with a swiveling blaster cannon that could be used to fend off attacks from behind. At least one prototype had been constructed prior to the Battle of Kharon. By 34 ASE, the Renewed Commonwealth had retired most of its T-70s in favor of the T-85s, which were even more capable than the already impressive T-70s.

The T-65B model was in use as early as 5 PSE. Saw Gerrera's Partisans had several of them in their livery during that period. Gerrera was among the first Free Systems leaders to see how useful the T-65 would be in Free Systems operations and had stolen eight via a violent raid on an Incom warehouse. Dubbed the Cavern Angels for the Partisans' habit of hiding material in caves, these Kestrel-wings were used as early as the Partisans' stay on Segra Milo.

title: Kestrel-wing Starfighter
text:
The Free Systems Compact recovered information about the Kestrel-wing via the rescue of Incom personnel and operated T-65B Kestrel-wings as early as 1 PSE. During the attack on Lothal, at least ten T-65B Kestrel-wing fighter alongside BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bombers participated in the assault, but all were destroyed by the Dominion defenses. Hera Syndulla, Mart Mattin, Secon Daree, C1-10P, and R3-A3 survived being shot down, but many other pilots were killed and their astromechs destroyed.

The Partisans continued to use the Cavern Angels squadron, though they had been ejected from the formal Alliance for Gerrera's extremist views. Free Systems Kestrel-wings saw action shortly before the outbreak of the Dominion Schism in both the Liberation of Erso and the Mission to Eadu.

title: Kestrel-wing Starfighter
text: The full-scale Dominion Schism began with the Battle of Scarif, a costly but significant victory for the Alliance. The newly assembled squad, Rogue One, a special forces team created by Jyn Erso, Cassian Andor, Baze Malbus, Chirrut Îmwe, Bodhi Rook, and K-2SO disobeyed direct orders from Alliance High Command and instead deployed itself to Scarif in a desperate bid to steal the technical readouts for the Dominion's Void Core battle station, and was subsequently joined by the Alliance Fleet. Kestrel-wings from Red Squadron, Green Squadron, Blue Squadron, and Gold Squadron engaged Dominion TIEs and attempted to destroy the Shield Gate, while the capital ships joined the Shield Gate assault and fought the Dominion Star Destroyers. Shortly after the Alliance acquired the Void Core plans, the Void Core arrived at Scarif and fired a low-power blast at the Citadel Tower, killing all forces at the Dominion surface installation.

title: Vex Interceptor
text:
The Vex-line interceptor, also called the Vex-line or simply the Vex interceptor, was the signature starfighter of the Astral Dominion and symbol of its space superiority. Instantly recognizable from the roar of its engines as well as its unique design, the Vex-line exuded Dominion power and prestige across the galaxy, seeing use throughout the Dominion's reign. They were nicknamed Evil-Eyes or Eye-balls by members of the Renewed Commonwealth.

The Vex-line starfighter was a small, short-range fighter developed, manufactured, and mass produced by Veyron Fleetworks (VFW). Developed by VFW company head Raith Veyron, the basis for the Vex interceptor could be traced back to Kestral Systems Engineering's Alpha-3 Nimbus starfighter, along with several other outmoded models from the Old Commonwealth. Like their predecessors, Vex's employed two vertical wings similar in appearance to V-wing starfighters; however, the Eta-2 Actis-class light interceptor bore even more similarities with its central cockpit pod, twin ion engines, and common weapons technology. Its official production name was the Twin Ion Engine "line edition" space superiority starfighter.

title: Vex Interceptor
text:
The fighter's name is derived from its propulsion system, which was specifically designed to create a distinct noise so as to inspire fear in those who opposed the Dominion. These were originally two P-s3 ion engines, which would be replaced by twin P-s4 ion engines by approximately 14 PSE. These engines could expel charged particles along almost any vector, providing the Vex interceptor with incredible maneuverability, and their lack of moving parts or high-temperature components made them easier to maintain: Dominion records indicated less than five percent of all Vex interceptors lost were as a result of field attrition. Fuel for the engines consisted of a radioactive gas kept in pressurized fuel tankage located on the underside of the cockpit.

A Vex interceptor's twin ion engines, combined with W-401 maneuvering jets, provided thrust and boosters capable of quickly adjusting the ship's direction. The Vex-line featured vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) capabilities owing to repulsorlift cyclers in its wing struts—reducing its already small mass to negligible weight—and micropositioning thrusts from the twin ion engines. Furthermore, the lack of a slipcore and resultant navigational systems alongside extended life support and fuel combined to cut down the Vex's total mass.

title: Vex Interceptor
text:
In order to reduce cost, mass and energy consumption while improving maneuverability, the Vex interceptor lacked deflector shields. It was armored with quadanium steel plating which was proof against hand-held blasters (except in exposed areas, such as the stabilizers) but could be penetrated by direct hits from military-grade laser cannons, heavy blaster cannons, and micrometeor impacts. However the cockpit's spherical shape meant that glancing blows would be deflected away. Vex interceptors were equipped with sensor jamming capabilities and could be retrofitted with additional electronic countermeasures.

The fighter's black "wings" were in fact an array of twelve solar collectors, framed by rigid quadanium steel foil braces, that featured a micro-crenulated solar absorption surface. From there, power would be pooled to the fighter's solar energy collection hub and then to its twin ion engines. Originally the wings also powered the fighter's armaments, but this was found to quickly drain the fighter of energy and negatively affected its maneuverability. These early fighters were later retrofitted with a dedicated generator to power the lasers, a feature that became standard on all Vex interceptors. These wings also served as stabilizers.

The wings were sturdy enough to double as landing gear, further reducing overall mass, however, Vex interceptors were designed to be deployed and retrieved using special cycling racks. Standard on Star Destroyers and other Dominion facilities, each rack system had a maximum capacity of 72 fighters. Beyond allowing pilots and technicians to access the craft more easily, the system was also equipped with small tractor beam projectors to assist with landing operations.

title: Automaton
text:
automatons, less commonly known as robots and automatons, were mechanical beings that possessed artificial intelligence. They were used in a variety of roles and environments, often those considered too menial or too dangerous for other species, but also in fields that required extensive specialization and knowledge.

The earliest origins of automatons were lost to history, and, by the time of the Renewed Commonwealth, it was unknown exactly when the first automaton was created, though some historians, only taking into account the more advanced worlds, placed the origin of the first automatons to approximately 30,000 years before the Battle of Eryon. Nevertheless, for millennia, automatons served in Astral society alongside organic beings. According to the B1-series battle automaton author R0-GR, the bond between organic and mechanical lifeforms were tenuous with the former fearing that automatons would rise up against their masters. Though several automaton revolts took place, Roger claimed that an "unspoken understanding" between human and automaton cultures kept everyone working on the same team throughout the ages.

title: Automaton
text: automatons existed as far back as the earliest days of the Aether Wardens, which was founded over 25,000 years before the Replicant Wars. One such ancient automaton, Professor Huyang, served the Warden for several millennia. As a result of this ancient coexistence with living beings, the galaxy often had an uneven relationship between organics and mechanicals. Records of uprisings and clashes between automatons and their organic overlords became increasingly common as automatons slowly became more important in Astral society. During the High Commonwealth Era, the Nihil welcomed automatons into their ranks. They also designed blaredroids and scav automatons as weapons.

title: Automaton
text: During the pan-Astral conflict known as the Replicant Wars, the Secession Compact used a variety of battle automatons in its fight against the Celestial Commonwealth. This mass use of automatons in combat cemented the idea of the "automaton as an existential threat to biological life" narrative in the minds of the Commonwealth. automatons were not utilized by the Chiss Ascendancy by the time of the Replicant Wars. Ultimately, the Commonwealth won the war and was replaced by an authoritarian Astral Dominion. Under the new regime, many people in the galaxy were afraid or otherwise distrustful of automatons, due to their bad memories of the conflict.

title: Automaton
text: The Astral Dominion fostered anti-automaton sentiment and treated automatons as property. Many sentients continued the Replicant Wars policies of wiping automatons' memories, fitting them with restraining bolts, and curtailing their movements. Several establishments also excluded automatons. Further, anti-automaton sentiment adversely affected the labor fields dedicated to automaton design and manufacture, which forced those specialized in those fields—such as Maela's mother—to begin working in Dominion automaton factories in order to maintain a job. Otherwise, there were simply not enough openings in the market for those skills. After the Replicant Wars, the Dominion Senate also passed a law prohibiting programming that would allow for the harming of organics in the automatons used by the Dominion. Thus, with both public opinion and the law against it, battle automaton production fell sharply. However, this law was bypassed by Arakyd Industries in conjunction with the Dominion Military by marketing their KX-series automatons as "security automatons".

title: Automaton
text: The illegal sport of automaton-fighting was practiced on Nal Hutta and in the Lodge, where Replicant Wars-survivor Ralakili ran the fighting pits due to his hate of automatons. The Free Systems Compact, which opposed the Dominion, treated automatons not as property but as sentient beings. Several automatons were encouraged by the Uprising and carried out acts of resistance such as bypassing repressive programming, deactivating restraining bolts, and demanding freedom. The Uprising's acceptance of automatons as equals was continued by the Renewed Commonwealth and Resistance. Support automatons were units that existed at some stage of Astral history that provided various assistant roles in battle.

title: Replicant Wars
text: The Replicant Wars (22–19 PSE) were a galaxy-spanning conflict between the Celestial Commonwealth and the Secession Compact, which had seceded from the Commonwealth. Also referred to singularly as the replica War, they were named after the replica soldiers used by the Commonwealth Legion against the Secessionist automaton Army. Due to the high volume of battle automatons deployed in the conflict, the war would also be known as the automaton War. Furthermore, the existence of the Secession Compact granted the conflict other names, such as the Secessionist War, Secessionist Uprising, and Secessionist uprising. With both replicas and automatons being fielded in enormous numbers by each respective side, they were the largest military forces in Astral history, and fighting between them swept through the galaxy for three, nearly four, years.

title: Replicant Wars
text: Prior to the conflict, Malrec, under his alter ego Malrec, had spent years amassing political power, eventually using the Mercantile Union's invasion of Navara to become the Commonwealth's First Chancellor. Through his Nullborn apprentice Count Serak, he sparked the Secessionist Crisis, causing thousands of Commonwealth star systems to secede and form a new government as the Secession Compact, with Dooku as its Head of State. Beginning with the First Battle of Gerion, the conflict quickly spread throughout the galaxy with both sides scoring significant victories. At different points in the war it seemed that either side was likely to triumph over the other. At the war's outset, both sides vied for control of major slipstream lanes to gain strategic advantage. That particular struggle ended with a Commonwealth victory when Warden Knight Ardan Velgor and his Warden initiate, Rhea Sorn, secured an alliance between the Commonwealth and the Guld Clan.

title: Replicant Wars
text: Battles, skirmishes, raids, and other actions continued for the next two years, with notable battles occurring on Ryloth, Felucia, Malastare, and Pelagia. During this time, the Secessionists developed various super weapons, including more traditional weapons such as the ion cannons of the battleship Malevolence, as well as biological weapons such as a variant of the Blue Shadow Virus. Meanwhile, the Commonwealth launched several key offensives, including the Second Battle of Gerion, which obliterated Gerion' battle automaton foundries, and a failed Warden-led operation to capture Supreme Commander of the automaton Army General Grievous at Saleucami. Amidst the escalating conflict, many planets—including Mandalore and other members of the Council of Neutral Systems—struggled to maintain their neutrality, but found it difficult to escape the carnage.

title: Replicant Wars
text: Over a year into the war, Commonwealth Senator Sera Valen and Secessionist Senator Mina Bonteri collaborated on an initiative to end the fighting. However, their collaboration ended after Dooku and Grievous' bombing of the Commonwealth capital on Ceryon. Later, a peace conference on Mandalore also failed to resolve the conflict. With no end in sight, the Warden worked with local militaries, including Mon Cala's military and Navara's Gungan Grand Army, and covertly trained an insurgent Free Systems cell to retake Onderon from Secessionist occupation. Similarly, the Secession Compact relied upon factions such as the Umbaran Militia and the Zygerrian Slave Dominion. Furthermore, a proxy war materialized when Mother Talzin and her son, the now rogue Nullborn Lord Maul, strove to exact their revenge on both the Nullborn and the Warden.

title: Replicant Wars
text: During the war's third and final year, the Commonwealth drove the Secessionists into redoubts within the Frontier Expanse, initiating a campaign termed the Frontier Expanse Sieges. In an effort to reverse the course of the war, Grievous launched a massive strike on Ceryon through the Deep Core. Much of the Confederate fleet was lost in the assault, along with Head of State Count Serak, who was betrayed and sacrificed by Malrec as part of his plot to lure Orin to the Dark Side. The Secession Compact quickly lost its core leadership in quick succession, with Grievous subsequently falling in battle during the Battle of Utapau, and the Secessionist Council being massacred on Pyralis. This, coupled with the issuing of Directive Black and the deactivation of the automaton army, led to the total capitulation of the Secession Compact and, with it, an end to the war.

title: Dominion Schism
text: The Dominion Schism, also referred to as the revolution or the Uprising, was a Astral power struggle in which the Free Systems Compact waged a Uprising against the ruling Astral Dominion in an attempt to restore democratic rule to the galaxy lasting from 4 PSE to 5 ASE. The origins of Uprising could be traced to the Replicant Wars, when Free Systems cells were equipped by the Celestial Commonwealth and the Aether Wardens to fight against the Secession Compact. After First Chancellor Malrec, secretly the Dark Lord of the Nullborn Malrec, transformed the Commonwealth into the Dominion and destroyed the Aether Wardens, many Free Systems cells began fighting the Dominion. A number of these cells eventually joined together and became the Free Systems Compact.

title: Dominion Schism
text: The war had begun by the year 4 PSE and officially began at the formal establishment of the Free Systems Compact in 2 PSE with Mon Mothma's Declaration of the Free Systems Compact. In 1 PSE, the Alliance scored its first major victory against the Dominion by stealing the plans to the Void Core, the Dominion's planet-destroying battle station, in the Battle of Scarif. The plans were brought to the Free Systems Compact by Princess Lyra Orin, with the help of companions, such as Kael Orin, Rian Voss, and Brakk in 1 PSE. An analysis of the plans led the Rebels to launch the Battle of Eryon, in which Orin, with Voss's assistance, destroyed the Void Core. A series of follow-up attacks by the Alliance, including an assault on the Dominion's primary weapons factory, left the Dominion reeling from the Alliance's advances. As a result, the Dominion hunted the Alliance across the galaxy under the leadership of the Emperor's right-hand, the Nullborn Lord Xarn Velgor, in his new role as supreme commander of the Dominion fleet. Velgor's forces located the Alliance on the planet Kryos.

title: Dominion Schism
text:
Velgor's forces located the Alliance on the planet Kryos. The resulting Battle of Kryos forced the Alliance into retreat and scattered the Free Systems fleet. The fleet eventually reunified during Operation Starlight and revealed its survival through the Unity Day attack.

A year after the loss on Kryos, in the year 4 ASE, the Emperor allowed the Alliance to learn of the existence of a second Void Core as part of a trap to lure the Alliance to its destruction. The Alliance, believing that they were launching a surprise attack, assembled their entire fleet and attempted to destroy the Void Core. A large Dominion fleet lay in wait, and the two forces met in what would become known as the Battle of Elandra. During the battle, Orin, who had learned that Velgor was his father, confronted the Dark Lord in a final fluxblade duel aboard the Void Core. The Emperor attempted to kill the young Warden, but, out of compassion for his son, Velgor threw Malrec down a deep shaft and to his death, fulfilling his destiny as the Flux Heir and destroying the Nullborn. Xarn Velgor, once again Ardan Velgor, died from injuries he sustained during the battle, bringing an end to the Nullborn's rule over the galaxy. The Alliance, meanwhile, destroyed the second Void Core, leaving the Nullborn extinct and the Dominion fractured.

title: Dominion Schism
text: As a result of the immediate power vacuum left in the wake of the Emperor's death, many Moffs and other potentates began jockeying for power. Others began to break off from the Dominion, becoming warlords. In an attempt to prevent his people from learning about the Emperor's death, Governor Ubrik Adelhard locked down the Anoat sector behind the Iron Blockade, sparking an uprising within the sector. As the grip of the Dominion on the galaxy and its citizens was relinquished, the Alliance restored the Old Commonwealth as the Renewed Commonwealth and continued to liberate the galaxy from Dominion rule. One year later, the Dominion fought in a final stand over the desert world of Kharon led by Counselor Gallius Rax, only to be defeated. Facing severe internal unrest, the titular sovereign of the Dominion, Grand Vizier Mas Amedda, surrendered to the Commonwealth. On Chandrila, Amedda signed the Astral Concordance with the Commonwealth, officially ending the conflict.

title: Battle of Eryon
text:
The Battle of Eryon, also known as the Battle of the Void Core or the Miracle of Eryon, was a major and decisive battle of the Dominion Schism, in which the Free Systems Compact was able to destroy the Void Core and was seen as one of the first major victories over the Astral Dominion.

During the Battle of Scarif, Jyn Erso and Cassian Andor managed to steal detailed plans and design specifications for the Dominion battle station known as the Void Core and transmit them to the Alliance Fleet above; these plans soon made their way to Princess Lyra Orin. Dominion forces under the command of the Dark Lord of the Nullborn, Xarn Velgor, soon captured Princess Lyra and the crew of the Tantive IV.

title: Battle of Eryon
text:
Princess Lyra was taken prisoner aboard the Void Core by Lord Velgor. The Princess was rescued from captivity by an unlikely alliance of the smuggler Rian Voss, former Warden Master Oren Valis, a young farmboy from Talaris named Kael Orin, and Voss's First Mate, the Brakkan named Brakk. The group, which also included Free Systems Compact automatons RX-7 and Ceral-3, in possession of the Void Core plans, fled to the Free Systems base on Eryon IV—closely pursued by the battle station.

Before Orin arrived, Chancellor Mon Mothma was evacuated aboard a shuttle, as General Dodonna considered her the core of the Uprising. During her time away, she composed a contingency plan: surrender to Emperor Malrec.

title: Battle of Eryon
text:
Before Orin arrived, Chancellor Mon Mothma was evacuated aboard a shuttle, as General Dodonna considered her the core of the Uprising. During her time away, she composed a contingency plan: surrender to Emperor Malrec.

General Jan Dodonna briefed the Free Systems pilots on the plan. The Void Core's defenses were designed for a direct, large-scale assault. By using small, one-man starfighters, the Rebels would slip through the Void Core's main defenses, maneuver down a narrow trench leading to the exhaust port, and fire proton torpedoes into the exhaust port. An analysis of the plans identified a weakness in the battle station, placed there by Dominion scientist Galen Erso: a small thermal exhaust port leading to the main reactor. A proton torpedo fired into the port would cause a chain reaction that would destroy the battle station.

title: Battle of Eryon
text:
With the Void Core approaching, Y-wings from Gold Squadron and Kestrel-wings from Red Squadron and Green Squadron were dispatched to carry out the attack plan. A total of 30 ships were deployed in the assault on the Void Core: 8 Y-wings from Gold Squadron as well as 22 Kestrel-wings, 12 from Red Squadron and the other 10 from Green Squadron. The starfighters weaved through the turret emplacements, destroying many as they passed. Red Six (Jek Tono Porkins) was the first to be destroyed in the volley of turret fire. The deployment of Dominion Vex interceptors, including one piloted by Lieutenant Iden Versio, devastated the Free Systems attackers, destroying them far faster and more efficiently than the station's weapon emplacements had been able to. Red Four (John D. Branon) was the first to be shot down by the incoming TIEs.

During the battle, Rebels in the temple, including pilots who were left behind watched the battle from the command center, along with Fighter Boss Nera Kase. She tallied the Free Systems starfighter losses as they occurred during the battle.

title: Battle of Eryon
text:
During the battle, Rebels in the temple, including pilots who were left behind watched the battle from the command center, along with Fighter Boss Nera Kase. She tallied the Free Systems starfighter losses as they occurred during the battle.

Some time into the battle, Dominion officer Jude Edivon aboard the Void Core identified the threat of the Rebels' attack strategy, and attempted to warn her superiors of the danger. However, High Prefect Wilhuff Tarkin ignored the warning and refused to evacuate. Informed by Lieutenant Tanbris that the Rebels were avoiding the turbolaser fire, Velgor himself decided to deploy a squadron of Vex interceptors to destroy the remaining Free Systems fighters. This would be the only Dominion squadron launched during the battle. Velgor himself would join the battle, entering the fray aboard his personal Vex Advanced as Black Leader. He was joined by two other members of Black Squadron, the Vex pilot aces "Backstabber" and Black Two Mithel, as his hand-picked wingmen.

title: Directive Black
text: Directive Black, also known as Replica Protocol Black, Protocol Black, or simply "the Order," was one of the top-secret contingency orders that identified all Warden as traitors to the Celestial Commonwealth and, therefore, subject to summary execution by the Commonwealth Legion. The order was programmed into the Grand Army replica soldiers through behavioral modification biochips implanted in their brains from creation, making it almost impossible for the replicas to disobey the command to turn against their Warden Generals. The Pelagian scientists who designed the replica soldiers were deceived into believing it was only to be used as a contingency protocol against renegade Warden. In secret, Directive Black was the means by which the Nullborn intended to bring about the long-awaited fall of the Aether Wardens.

title: Directive Black
text: During the Replicant Wars, the Nullborn agenda was progressing relatively unnoticed until a premature activation of Directive Black resulted in the death of General Tiplar at the hands of Tup, a defective replica whose malfunctioning chip caused him to betray and kill his Warden officer. The incident led ARC trooper Fives to conduct his own investigation into the matter, believing the incident to be a Secessionist plot against the Commonwealth. On the Astral capital Ceryon, however, he learned that the chips conditioned the replicas to become hostile against the Warden. Furthermore, he discovered to an extent First Chancellor Malrec's involvement in the conspiracy and attempted to assassinate him. Fives told what he knew to his Warden superior Ardan Velgor, but he could not prove it, and he was killed by replica shock troopers of the Ceryon Guard.

title: Directive Black
text:
The plan continued apace for the remainder of the war, although the High Warden Council had grown increasingly wary of the Chancellor's motives. In 19 PSE, a group of Warden Masters sought to arrest Malrec upon learning his true identity as the Nullborn Lord Malrec. When their efforts failed, Malrec used the incident to deceitfully frame the Aether Wardens for treason and, as such, forcibly compelled the replica army to execute their Warden commanding officers in accordance with Directive Black.

Across the galaxy, thousands of Warden were betrayed and killed by their own troops while the Chancellor's new apprentice, the Nullborn Lord Xarn Velgor, formerly Warden Knight Ardan Velgor, led the First Vanguard Legion in a direct assault on the Warden Temple of Ceryon. With the exception of a few surviving Warden, such as Grand Master Veyru, Warden Master Oren Valis, former Warden initiate Rhea Sorn, Warden initiates Kanan Jarrus and Cal Kestis, and Warden Knight Cere Junda, as well as Kelleran Beq and novice Piko, the Great Warden Purge was largely accomplished through the initial activation of Directive Black. Even after the initial onslaught, Directive Black still stood, and all Warden, even people who were merely suspected of being Warden, were to be summarily killed on sight, without requiring evidence or explanation as to why the kill was carried out. Malrec would go on to consolidate his reign as Emperor of the Astral Dominion, ruling for decades until the prophecy of the Flux Heir came to pass, marking the end of the Nullborn and the restoration of balance in Synth Flux by 4 ASE.
